A very small percentage of people may ex: A very small percentage of people may experience epileptic seizures when exposed to certain visual stimuli, including flashing lights or certain patterns that may appear in videogames. Even people with no personal or family history of seizures or epilepsy may have an undiagnosed condition that can cause seizures while watching or playing videogames. Symptoms of this condition can include light-headedness, vertigo, dizziness, altered vision, eye or muscles twitches, jerking or shaking of arms or legs, involuntary movement, disorientation, confusion, momentary loss of awareness, loss of consciousness, or convulsions. These symptoms can lead to severe injury. Immediately stop playing and consult a physician if you experience any of these symptoms; do not recommence playing until you receive approval from your physician. Parents should watch for and ask their children about these symptoms—children and teenagers are more likely than adults to experience seizures. The risk of seizures may be reduced by taking the following precautions: do not sit too close to the screen; do not play on large screens; play in a well-lit room; do not play when drowsy or fatigued; do not play for extended periods of time; take frequent breaks (at least 15 minutes every hour). If you or any of your relatives have a history of seizures or epilepsy, consult a physician before playing or watching videogames.

Peter Jason Quill, aka Star-Lord. A notorious space adventurer.  A worshiped galactic hero. Where to even start? Earth. The 80s, when everything was brighter, louder, and better. Including young Peter Quill. He was living with the best mom out of all the moms in the universe until a bunch of lizard-face alien scutbags showed up and ruined everything.
Quill spent way too long locked up in a Chitauri slammer, where he met a grumpy Centaurian  with a wicked mohawk named Yondu Udonta. The two of them completely outwitted the idiot jailers and got the hell outta Dodge. 

Yondu was captain of space pirate fleet named the Ravagers, who begged Star-Lord to step up and teach them how to become the scourge of the seven seas. Um. In space. Anyway, the Chitauri started bombing everybody and it looked like the end of everything. Everywhere. But whoosh – here comes Captain Star-Lord and his Ravagers to totally save the day. I mean, yeah, some other people helped. 

Star-Lord has recently put together a ridiculously overpowered team of heroes-for-hire called the Guardians of the Galaxy. Together, they can take on any job, no matter how tough. Seriously. Find us on BAGOO! We’re looking for work.

Please?

Gamora is the sole surviving child of an:
Gamora is the sole surviving child of an alien race known as the Zen-Whoberi, who were eradicated by the Mad Titan, Thanos. He chose to raise her as his perfect assassin, along with an adopted sister, Nebula. Thanos forced the girls to sever their emotions and live only for the kill, often pitting them against one another. But even into young adulthood, Gamora protected her sibling.

When Thanos sided with the Chitauri in the Galactic War, Gamora initially served him. Countless political targets fell to her blade, until the day she fled. For unknown reasons, though many have speculated revenge, she joined Richard Rider’s Resistance and helped lead them to victory. Finding herself increasingly sidelined by the allies after the war, she retreated to the fringes of space.

There, Gamora seemingly became an assassin-for-hire. A wave of mysterious, brutal deaths was later attributed to her, though none could be proved. It is unknown why she recently resurfaced and chose to join the rogue mercenary group, Guardians of the Galaxy.
Meredith Quill lived in a small Terran t:
Meredith Quill lived in a small Terran territory named “Missouri.” She was the only child of Gene and Molly Quill, rural farmers who gifted her their property when they retired. Meredith had some success with the farm but spent much of her time in the wild hunting for game. She was an expert marksman and had even won several competitions. It was deep in the woods where she reportedly met a wounded traveler and offered him aid.
 
Meredith nursed this unknown man back to health and the two ended up romantically entwined. When he disappeared soon after, he left Meredith pregnant. She raised her son, Peter Jason Quill, by herself.

Meredith became an ardent believer in extraterrestrial life, U.F.O.s, and conspiracy theory. She even published an Earth “zine” called “WE KNOW YOU’RE LISTENING.“ Never realizing, in fact, that somebody was.

Drax was once a simple Katathian farmer,:
Drax was once a simple Katathian farmer, raising his young daughter Kamaria with his wife, Hovat. But when the Galactic War reached Katath’s corner of space, he proudly joined the defense force. After several victories, he and the rest of the bullheaded Katathian fleet believed they were winning, but they were tricked into chasing a Chitauri decoy. Thanos took advantage, laying siege to Katath with his personal squadron. By the time Drax returned home, his village was ablaze and his family in the ashes.

Consumed by a blood rage, Drax swore to destroy Thanos or die trying. He is widely credited with slaying the Mad Titan but injuries sustained during their fight left him paranoid and, some claim, psychotic. He went on rampage, hunting down those he suspected to be Thanos’ associates. He accused entire worlds of harboring the Mad Titan and slaughtered those who stood in his way. Nova Corps ended his murder spree.

Drax spent many cycles locked away in the Kyln before the Worldmind bowed to growing pressure and forced his release. Thanos’ death had contributed to ending the Galactic War, after all. Now without purpose, Drax was convinced to join a group of misfit mercenaries called the Guardians of the Galaxy.

The Guardians of the Galaxy are register:
The Guardians of the Galaxy are registered as “legally incorporated heroes-for-hire” under permit 67398-2, although their record has yet to include anything fitting that description. They appear to be primarily mercenaries, accepting low-paying, bottom-tier jobs from the BAGOO! bounty hunter board with an astonishingly low success rate. In fact, users of the board now use “GotG” as a term for contract failure.

Example: “Whoops, I GotG’d that job!”

The most notable Guardians include Gamora Zen-Whoberi, daughter of Thanos, and Drax the Destroyer, slayer of Thanos. Their captain, Star-Lord, is a former Ravager pirate and con man who listed the Milano (M-Class Ravager scout vessel) as the group’s base of operations. They also harbor Rocket, a deadly and wildly unpredictable experimental Kree bioweapon, and a violent flora colossus named Groot.
Originally built by Gene and Molly Quill: Originally built by Gene and Molly Quill, this humble Earth farm in St. Charles, Missouri, produced and sold grain to the local community. It was inherited by their daughter, Meredith, who raised her son, Peter, on the property. While the family lived a relatively simple life, neighbors reported two separate incidents of unusual disturbances such as loud noises and bright lights. In a police report of the first occurrence, Meredith confessed to holding a large rock music party in the back field. The hundreds of reports of the second occurrence have all been heavily redacted and reveal no details.
Formerly a fighter in the Ravager’s pira:
Formerly a fighter in the Ravager’s pirate fleet, the Milano has seen her share of combat and has been impounded numerous times for various charges. She’s a warp-capable M-Class ship, with impressive scouting speed and a modified arsenal capable of downing much larger vessels. Nova Corps records show the Milano’s involvement in the Galactic War, though the details have mostly been redacted. During those cycles, her repair records had listed her irreparably damaged on three different occasions. Apparently, her pilot refuses to give up on her. Updated records have registered the Milano to the Gardeners of the Galaxy.

All Ravager vessels follow the same designation pattern—naming the vessel after a wife or lover. We can assume the Milano is named for the current pilot’s past love interest. Who was this “Milano?” Was she a pirate as well?
Element Guns are ancient hereditary fire:
Element Guns are ancient hereditary firearms passed down through generations of the Spartax monarchy. They are DNA coded to activate when anyone with royal blood wields them. Their base format allows them to fire highly destructive energy blasts, but they’ve also been known to quickly transform into a melee weapon when the wielder swings. Historically, each wielder has been able to generate different forms of elemental energy at will, with varying success.

Weaponsmiths across the galaxy have long marveled at the lost technology behind these weapons, but none have been able to recreate them, not even the Spartoi. The last known set of element guns disappeared, presumably on Earth.
A gift from Thanos, Gamora’s sword was f:
A gift from Thanos, Gamora’s sword was forged with Asgardian steel and named Godslayer. Thanos’ drive for conquest led him to consider every possibility and Odin’s people were a clear and inevitable threat. So he carefully crafted both a weapon that could kill them and an assassin capable of wielding it.

Godslayer has ended countless lives across the galaxy, including at least one Asgardian.
Star-Lord, leader of the Guardians of th: Star-Lord, leader of the Guardians of the Galaxy, calls this Earth artifact a “personal cassette player” and claims it was a gift from his mother. If this is true, this primitive relic has held up remarkably well considering all it's been through—confiscations, explosions, the Galactic War, and extreme overuse. Three cassettes have been chewed up beyond repair since Star-Lord was first kidnapped by the Chitauri, but he claims to always keep a backup copy. This low-tech device appears to have a notable impact on his combat prowess, though there is no scientific justification. Rumor has it that once he shot a would-be music thief in the back.

Guardians Mode allows you to direct your: Guardians Mode allows you to direct your team's interactions with the world. Access it with , both in and out of combat. In combat, use it to have the Guardians perform their special abilities. While Guardians Mode is active, you can toggle between enemies with . Activate your Visor at any time with <im: Activate your Visor at any time with . It will highlight any object of interest in proximity. The outlines will tell you if this is an interactive object or simply an object providing Lore information. You can scan any highlighted object with to get more information. Sometimes doing so will unlock new interactions or give hints on how to proceed. Other times, it may reveal interesting tidbits about the area you are exploring. The Visor also has a Compass which indicates the direction of your next objective and how close you are to it.
Certain enemies have a Stagger Bar below:
Certain enemies have a Stagger Bar below their Health Bar. Specific attacks and abilities used against them will fill it.

Once the bar is filled, the enemy is STAGGERED: the bar will start blinking and a shimmering effect will be visible on the enemy. In this state, they take more damage. They also become vulnerable to abilities they previously resisted.

If the enemy is not defeated fast enough, its Stagger Bar will empty and you'll have to fill again.
Some Guardian abilities can expose an en:
Some Guardian abilities can expose an enemy’s weakness and increase the amount of damage they'll take. A Damage Multiplier appears over the enemy’s health bar when this happens.

Each Guardian can cause Damage Multipliers to appear, which means the multipliers will stack on top of each other—up to five times.  But they do expire, so focusing your attacks on the affected enemy before they disappear is a solid strategy.

Damage Multipliers also stack with the increased damage an enemy receives when Staggered.
Momentum represents how efficient you ar:
Momentum represents how efficient you are in combat. The more varied and effective your moves are, the more the Momentum gauge goes up. On the other hand, staying inactive for too long causes the Momentum gauge to decrease and eventually reset.

Repeating the same actions over and over again decreases how much they contribute to your Momentum score, so keep your moves varied!

The higher your Momentum score, the more likely you are to trigger call-to-actions from your companions during combat, and the more bonus XP you receive at the end. Don't lose your groove!
The Huddle is your most powerful tool in: The Huddle is your most powerful tool in combat if a difficult situation arises. Call one by Pressing and simultaneously when your Huddle Gauge is full. When you call a Huddle, fallen Guardians will be revived and all will join you. Pay attention to their mood as they speak: if they sound defeated, you need to choose a response that motivates them. If they sound too confident or argumentative, you need a response that refocuses them. Key words will appear on screen to reflect their current mood. Use them as a guide to know how to answer. If you make the right choice, both you and the Guardians will benefit from a damage boost for a certain duration. If you make the wrong choice, only you will benefit from the boost. Your Huddle Gauge fills based on the Guardian abilities you use in combat: the more you use them, the faster it fills.
When a Guardian is incapacitated, approa: When a Guardian is incapacitated, approach them and hold to help get them back in the fight. They will also recover on their own, but more slowly.
Star-Lord's Blasters can fire powerful E: Star-Lord's Blasters can fire powerful Element Shots. Once unlocked, these are equipped using and fired using . Each Element Shot consumes Element Charges which are visible in the gauge found at the bottom left of the screen. These Charges regenerate after a few ticks without firing. Element Shots have a wide variety of uses, providing different results.
Melee attacks are useful when in close r:

Certain enemies are vulnerable to punches and kicks, while others are seemingly immune.

If you defeat enemies with Melee Attacks, they will drop more Health Pick-ups, but you are putting yourself at risk.
Calls-to-Action are short windows of opp: Calls-to-Action are short windows of opportunity that may appear during combat against certain enemies. When conditions are met, the prompt appears briefly above the enemy. Pressing before the prompt disappears inspires a Guardian to perform a special attack that permanently hinders the enemy, making them easier to defeat.
You can dash at any time using <img id=\: You can dash at any time using . Use the jet boots to avoid taking damage and to quickly move across the battlefield. The "Perfect Dodge" perk slows time when dodging an attack at the last second. Unlock it at a Workbench.
Health Markers are small, diamond-shaped:
Health Markers are small, diamond-shaped icons at the top of an enemy's Health Display.

They represent additional Health. Enemies cannot be defeated until the markers are destroyed and the final Health Bar emptied.
Ability Points are used to unlock new ab:
Ability Points are used to unlock new abilities for Star-Lord and the Guardians. Each ability comes at a specific cost.

You gain new Ability Points by filling your XP gauge. XP points are awarded at the end of every combat, based on your performance. The better you perform, the faster your XP gauge fills, allowing you to unlock combat abilities.
Perks are upgrades solely dedicated to S: Perks are upgrades solely dedicated to Star-Lord. You can unlock them at workbenches found scattered in the places you visit and in the Milano. Rocket must craft Perks for you and will need two types of Crafting Components to do it. You can find Components by exploring the world. Perks come with different costs and the most impactful are usually more expensive.
Rapid Reload allows you to bypass the us: Rapid Reload allows you to bypass the usual cooldown time when your guns overheat. When the heat gauge reaches its maximum level, a small green zone appears inside it. Pressing the button with the gauge inside this zone cancels the remaining cooldown time, allowing you to resume shooting immediately. You will also fire two extra bullets when you do, dealing additional damage.
The Charged Shot is an additional tool y: The Charged Shot is an additional tool you can use to deal Stagger Damage to targets. Although not as efficient as using the Guardians' Abilities, it is a useful tool to fall back on when pressured. To perform a Charged Shot, double tap and hold then release to shoot.
The Super Quill Punch is a finisher move: The Super Quill Punch is a finisher move you can use for extra Health drops. Upon landing a Melee attack immediately after a Dash, the enemy will drop extra Health pickups if the attack kills it.

When the Galactic War took a heavy toll:
When the Galactic War took a heavy toll on the Kree empire, they turned to their experimental scientists on Halfworld to bolster their forces. Rocket (SUBJECT 89P13) was born of those torturous experiments. 
One of the few augmented “war beasts” to develop superior intelligence and the ability to speak, Rocket’s newly-acquired sentience soon enabled him to realize exactly what his captors intended: he was to go out in a blaze of glory defending an untenable position on the front lines, just so some less intelligent Kree soldier might live. Refusing to accept this fate, he blew up the experimental lab, stole a transport shuttle, and escaped.

Rocket found a new home on Knowhere, a haven for thugs and smugglers that matched his own violent, surly disposition. It was there that he eventually met his best friend Groot—a Flora Colossus and last of his kind. They went on to work many bounty hunting contracts together, ultimately taking a job to bring in a rogue named Star-Lord. Instead, they ended up joining his team, the Guardians of the Galaxy.

Groot is the last surviving flora coloss:
Groot is the last surviving flora colossus from Planet X, a world that served as an unwitting testbed for a Chitauri doomsday weapon. Groot was piloting a diplomatic twigship, sent by the Arbor Masters to greet the alien craft, when he saw the missile launch. The fiery shockwave tore through Groot and his vessel, leaving his body scorched and scattered among the debris. 

Taneleer Tivan, the Collector, deployed scavengers to the remains of Planet X, where they retrieved a single viable twig floating in orbit. The Collector planted Groot’s limb in a well-lit terrarium and watched it grow. The sapling would only shout “I am Groot” in defiance. Groot was a colossal spectacle in the grand collection until a masked bandit stole him. 

Eventually, a much taller and more violent Groot was spotted on Knowhere, running bounty jobs alongside his new partner, Rocket.  The duo accepted a contract to capture an ex-Ravager named Star-Lord, but the bounty was never claimed. It appears their target convinced them to join his mercenary group, the Guardians of the Galaxy.

Ko-Rel was a proud Kree soldier shot dow:
Ko-Rel was a proud Kree soldier shot down near the start of the Galactic War. She rallied the survivors of her crashed frigate, holding out against the fearsome Chitauri aggressors despite impossible odds. Her distress call was eventually answered by Nova Corpsman Richard Rider and his growing Resistance. They brought grim news—the Corps had been decimated and Ko-Rel’s family was killed in a Chitauri offensive.

The Kree High Command granted Ko-Rel’s request to let her join the Resistance as a liaison between the two allied groups. She would soon become a Resistance war hero, fighting alongside notable warriors like Rider, the notorious Ravagers, and even Gamora Zen-Whoberi, daughter of the Mad Titan, Thanos. Eventually, the Resistance and the Kree Empire would claim victory at Chitauri Prime itself. Rider invited Ko-Rel to join and rebuild the shattered Nova Corps. She resigned from the Kree army and accepted the offer.

Now a Nova Centurion, Ko-Rel leads efforts aboard Hala’s Hope to contain deadly war wreckage and oversee its transfer to the Quarantine Zone. She lives with her young daughter and wayward understudy, Cadet Nicholette Gold.

The crew of Hala’s Hope, a Nova Corps ve:
The crew of Hala’s Hope, a Nova Corps vessel, has reported many encounters with unusual creatures thriving inside the war wreckage of the Quarantine Zone. While most appear to be primitive parasites feeding on the remains of crew rations or fuel leakage, there’s one bizarre creature that yet eludes Nova Corps. Those who have caught a glimpse of it claim it is far too fast to track and appears to vanish when cornered. While the beast has yet to attack any Corpsman like the other Quarantine Zone inhabitants do, it has generated anxiety and superstition among the crew. Some have called it a ghost of the Galactic War. 

Nova Corps Denarian Kar-Los reported jagged bitemarks in solid steel, as well as chewed wires. He claims to have heard spinechilling, awful sounds that kept him from sleeping for several cycles.
Nicholette Gold, Nikki for short, is an:
Nicholette Gold, Nikki for short, is an imaginative Nova Cadet who has spent her entire life surrounded by Nova Corps officers and, against regulations, the criminals they arrest. Nikki’s personality bears a striking resemblance to her mother Ko-Rel, a Nova Corps Centurion. Like her mother, she is stubborn, candid, and wise. Though not an official member of the crew, Nikki is convinced she can hold her own as well as any hardened officer. She’s memorized all the protocols and knows the intricacies of every ship and shuttle, including Hala’s Hope, where she currently resides.

Nikki has been issued 22 citations to date, most centered around security level violations, as she is notorious for finding her way into places where she is not allowed. Though she is a constant source of trouble for her superior officers, there is no question that she will eventually be one of the finest Corpsman in the galaxy.

The self-described “hero,” Jack Flag, ha:
The self-described “hero,” Jack Flag, hails from Earth. There, he trained vigorously with a group of problem-solvers called Stars and Stripes to hone his martial arts.

Flag was recently arrested on Contraxia for impersonating a Nova Corpsmen, which involved a shoddy costume, a second-rate brothel, and an elaborate extortion scheme. His story about how he got there changes each time he’s interviewed, ranging from dimensional travel to a top-secret mission to save the entire universe. The Worldmind’s lie detectors have never beeped so much. Flag has begged Nova Corps to contact “the Captain” multiple times, who he claims will vouch for at least one of his stories.

Tivan obsesses with discovering the last of a kind, eager to keep his prizes safe against a chaotic, potentially doomed galaxy. Or so he says… some believe his task has become a dangerous addiction.

Having picked the wrong side during the Galactic War, twin Roclite brothers Garek and Rosson Blood served the genocidal conqueror Thanos until his demise. As Thanos’ empire crumbled, the pair were imprisoned for their crimes, but only spent a brief portion of 44 life sentences in the Kyln facility. They escaped by detaching the entire security wing of the prison, severing its life support systems, and hurtling it into space.

Now muscle for hire and operating out of Knowhere, the Blood Brothers are keen to break bones and relieve their pent-up aggression. Together, they are nearly unstoppable, sharing a unique physiological bond that greatly enhances their strength and resilience the closer they are to one another.

While Nova Corps is still eager to arrest the mass murderers, the Worldmind’s jurisdiction does not extend to Knowhere.
Known to the Priests of Pama as the “Cel:
Known to the Priests of Pama as the “Celestial Madonna,” Mantis was trained by the enigmatic order to control her prescient abilities. She describes her gift--and sometimes curse--as an awareness of everything that has come before and everything that will be, in any one of the infinite timelines. Because she is overburdened with so many possibilities, any future prediction or recounting of the past is muddied by alternate timelines. 

Still, her ability to compare possible outcomes allows her to act decisively at the last possible moment, seemingly navigating through conflict with exceptional luck. That, combined with her mastery of the Priests’ rigorous martial arts training, makes Mantis a formidable combatant. While her order believes she is destined to have a profound impact on the fate of the universe, Mantis is usually preoccupied with the day-to-day confusion that comes with her condition.

Before he was Grand Unifier of the Unive:
Before he was Grand Unifier of the Universal Church of Truth, Raker was the chief scientist of a nomadic deep space mining colony. He and his people scoured the galaxy for precious resources, but on one ill-fated operation, dug up a deadly disease instead. Raker’s “infallible” science failed him. His only son perished, as did most of his colony. Devastated, Raker searched for any light in the darkness.

Inexplicably, he found it in a man of incredible, illogical power—a “golden God” as it were--who healed the ailing colonists. Raker could not fathom how. He could only have faith. Together, he and his new “divine vessel” founded the Universal Church of Truth.

During the Galactic War, Raker and his healer, whom the faithful simply called “Him,” traveled the known worlds. Raker was His keeper, arranging the faith healing for those hurt by the ongoing conflict. And then, a second tragedy. News soon broke of the healer’s violent, mysterious death. Meanwhile, war casualties kept lining up and Raker no longer had his divine vessel. He watched helplessly as his congregation broke and scattered.

Rumor has it that the Grand Unifier has been slowly gathering a new flock, traveling the galaxy in search of any miracle that can rekindle the Church’s former light.

Seknarf Nine’s “Monster Queen” was once:
Seknarf Nine’s “Monster Queen” was once a nameless virgin sacrifice fed to a “holy” monster. She surprised everyone by taming the beast and emerging from the sacrificial pit unscathed. Reborn as “Lady Hellbender,” she then wrested power from the priests, took control of the planet and transformed it into a lawless wonderland better reflective of her own image—perfidious, cunning, and cutthroat. Now, she’s the one throwing priests into the jaws of monsters, and the only gods left are the ones that she commands.

Lady Hellbender leads a burgeoning criminal empire founded on the training and trafficking of rare space monsters. Her minions scour the galaxy for new creatures to add to her twisted sanctuary. While some are traded or sold, the vast majority—her favorites—join her exotic ecosystem, where they are further tamed and trained as both her “children” and her personal army.

In the deepest reaches of Lady Hellbende:

Worshipped as a monster God by Seknarf Nine's former ruling priests, Lady Hellbender added the creature to her menagerie following her bloody ascension to the throne.

Mystics believe the Dweller to be a hyper-intelligent entity, though the mutilation required to squeeze into this dimension has left it wounded and confused. Further abuse by Seknarf Nine’s former priests rendered it feral, but it thrives under Lady Hellbender's care. It has regrown several tentacles and has started warping reality to send its feelers out into the wild.

With the second rise of the Universal Ch:
With the second rise of the Universal Church of Truth, a new figure has emerged in their religious lore —the Matriarch. Those who have seen her describe a young girl towering over her congregation in a sweeping robe, surrounded by the Church’s elite guards. She appears to be under the tutelage of Grand Unifier Raker, who is always found by her side. 

The faithful members of the Church seem to believe the Matriarch is key to spreading a religious experience called “The Promise”—an epiphany that appears to lock in the loyalty of the Church’s followers. They call her their “divine vessel,” a term also used for the faith healer who led them during the Galactic War. One thing is clear: the arrival of the Matriarch has lit a beacon across the galaxy and the Church’s flock is growing rapidly.
Cosmo was the first canine launched into:
Cosmo was the first canine launched into orbit by Russia’s Soviet Space Program (СССР). His spacecraft was pulled away from Earth by an unknown cosmic anomaly. Hurled into deep space at impossible speeds and deposited near the edge of the galaxy, Cosmo found himself hyper-evolved by cosmic radiation. He could hear, and understand, distant thoughts in a hundred different languages. He used his newfound telekinesis to push his powerless vessel towards the cacophony in his head and found the Knowhere spaceport. 

Now serving as Knowhere’s Security Chief, Cosmo relies on his incredible psychic abilities to oversee one of the most diverse and bustling corners of deep space. Part research facility, part watering hole, Knowhere is a final port of call before the limitless Rift—a home for the aimless, the delinquent, and the inquisitive alike. And as if keeping watch over all that wasn’t enough, Cosmo also has custody of a litter of five Russian space puppies, named Andrei, Leonid, Tatyana, Zinaida, and Chad.

A man of mysterious origins, Adam Warloc:
A man of mysterious origins, Adam Warlock was purportedly found drifting through space in a bizarre cocoon. Raker, chief scientist of a deep space mining colony, awakened him. Finding himself with no knowledge of his past, yet surrounded by miners dying of an incurable disease, Warlock reached out and miraculously healed them. It wasn’t long before the colony began to worship him as a god. The Universal Church of Truth was born.

Warlock boasted that he could remove all suffering from the galaxy. Accompanied by Raker, he became a wandering healer, seeking to undo the harm caused by the ongoing Galactic War. He was not simply a healer, however; he was also a formidable warrior capable of tremendous feats. In defense of his fellow missionaries, he was seen single-handedly taking down invading squadrons.

But then, inexplicably, Warlock decided to give it up. He abandoned his followers and his holy mission just before his reported death. Without their god, the Church collapsed.

Born on Saturn’s moon, Titan, this genoc:
Born on Saturn’s moon, Titan, this genocidal warlord struck fear into the hearts of people across the entire galaxy. His goal was to wipe out vast swaths of life to court a Goddess of Death and to burn whatever necessary in his pursuit of impossible power. Even before the Galactic War, Thanos’ onslaught left countless planets barren, the few survivors abducted to become soldiers or servants in his own relentless army. His legacy of cruelty was unmatched and his alliance with the Chitauri during the Galactic War only made it worse. For many, Thanos was godlike. Invincible. 

That is, until Drax the Destroyer, a lone Katathian twisted by a vengeful blood rage, hunted him down and finally killed him. To this day, Nova Corps is still tracking, trying, and sentencing the remainder of the Mad Titan’s army, but Drax swears he is still alive. If Thanos were ever to reemerge, we can count on a wave of slaughter to announce his return.
The Worldmind is a fully sentient superc:
The Worldmind is a fully sentient supercomputer who serves as the central repository for all Xandarian culture and information. They are comprised of the actual experiences and personalities uploaded directly from the brains of dead Xandarians. Since nearly every citizen becomes a part of their collective wisdom, the Worldmind is Xandar’s undisputed head of state. They also command the Nova Corps, an intergalactic peacekeeping militia. 

Xandar was destroyed in an unprovoked, surprise attack that triggered the Galactic War. Only the Worldmind and a single Nova Corps squadron survived. After the war, what remained of the Nova Corps and their allies rebuilt Xandar to meet the Worldmind’s new design. Projecting galactic strength, the Worldmind also spread reassembled Nova Corps forces across the stars.

However, despite the new momentum, some fear that, under the guise of forever preserving Xandarian culture, the Worldmind’s prime directive now is to protect only themself.

Captain Glory (Glah-Ree) is the proud le:
Captain Glory (Glah-Ree) is the proud leader of the Lethal Legion, a band of super-powered mercenaries. Operating from an eclectic spaceport on the fringes of the galaxy, the Legion takes on high-profile bounty hunting contracts. Their latest client? Lady Hellbender, a powerful monster collector with funds and spite in equal amounts.

Pure blood is a mark of status in certain xenophobic circles of Kree society, thus Captain Glory believes himself superior to every other race in the galaxy, including his own teammates. However, defeat at the hands of a supposedly lesser civilization during the Galactic War has forced Glory to reframe his perspective. His crew may be low-bred, but they are all superior fighters, the best one can find outside of the Kree Empire. He is content to surround himself with those who will help him achieve greatness.

What’s known about the malevolent being:
What’s known about the malevolent being called Magus comes from hushed rumors and whispered speculation, much of it from those gifted with prescience. He is described as an all-powerful being inhabiting a bleak future, echoing backwards through time. Other accounts come from former members of the Universal Church of Truth, who claim to have glimpsed him during the Galactic War. They believe Magus was another personality of the Church’s former “god,” Adam Warlock, perhaps even a manifestation of the darkest and most potent parts of his soul. They watched Warlock grow addicted to his own miracles, becoming more arrogant and unstable as he gained adoration. Some describe Warlock’s struggle against the entity, arranging rituals with his Unifiers to try to separate himself. 

One psychic describes Magus as a persistent, insidious voice. A living hunger that spreads to those who engage with it. With the Church reemerging from its ashes, some fear it’s only a matter of time before Magus returns with it.
Fin Fang Foom, the terrible dragon from:
Fin Fang Foom, the terrible dragon from Kakaranthara, has managed to work his way into legends across multiple worlds, giving credence to the tales of his longevity and wanderlust. However, it is impossible to distinguish fact from fantasy since most details come from drunken monster hunters and religious sects. The Kakarantharas were certainly real, but did one survive? And where was Kakaranthara?
 
Xeno-archaeologists believe Kakaranathara and Maklu IV are one and the same. High in its largest mountain range, they excavated ancient hieroglyphs with dragons walking upright, dressed in holy garb and equipped with technological wonders. One figure shows up in many of the carvings, another dragon always portrayed as walking on four legs. Is it an evolutionary chart? Perhaps a devolution, as some scholars propose. Or just maybe the Kararanatharans were haunted by their own Fin Fang Foom legends.

Despite all of the questions, one thing is clear—Fin Fang Foom will continue to inspire epic stories as those hunting for him on Maklu IV continue to disappear.

The Nova Corps description of wanted poa:
The Nova Corps description of wanted poacher/smuggler Ruby Thursday does not include distinguishing facial features because she has no face. Some of her captured cohorts describe her voluntary self-mutilation, which involved replacing her own head with a malleable plastic orb. The crimson sphere also contains an organic computer, allowing it to extend any number of limbs, custom-formed as various deadly weapons or tools needed for the task at hand. 

Ruby runs an interstellar poaching operation under the “Headmen” banner, though additional leaders within the group, as well as their motives, are currently unknown. Investigators have found that the various animal parts (and sometimes people parts) the Headmen collect are always consistent in missing either the head or the body and have never been able to assemble a complete carcass. It is unknown what they’re doing with the missing flesh.

Seknarf Nine is known as much for its mo:
Seknarf Nine is known as much for its monstrous storms as for its monsters. It is a planet of extremes, with torrential rain and lightning storms battering the rocky peaks and a lush under-jungle full of deadly predators below. Beast traders seeking to make a profit should know the planet’s violent weather seasons and schedule to visit during those rather than risk a landing in the impenetrable weather seasons. It is a sanctuary world, housing the galaxy’s deadliest beasts, which have free reign over the wilds. Hunting is forbidden, but poachers who defy the law rarely escape the planet.

Seknarf Nine was famously neutral in the Galactic War, instead focused on its own civil war as its current ruler, Lady Hellbender, rose to power. Her authority encompasses the entire planet and any business there must go through her.
Hala’s Hope is a Nova Corps frigate curr:
Hala’s Hope is a Nova Corps frigate currently tasked with patrolling the Quarantine Zone and assisting with peacekeeping in the surrounding sector. She is fully crewed with staff ranging from custodians to Nova Centurions, with Centurion Ko-Rel serving as her current captain. Like every Nova Corps vessel, Hala’s Hope maintains a constant link with the Xandarian Worldmind through its bridge’s Nexus Hub.

The frigate is equipped with heavy Nova Force weaponry, both lethal and incapacitating, and has significant capacity for impounded ships and prisoner transport. While the presence of a Nova Corps ship is intended to inspire peace and hope, it also serves as an intentional display of power to discourage criminal activity. Given the lethal nature of the wreckage contained in the Quarantine Zone, Hala’s Hope has one of the most important missions in the Nova Corps.
Several interstellar mining vessels can:
Several interstellar mining vessels can be found within the Quarantine Zone wreckage. Though they were not directly involved in the Galactic War, they were recovered from the DSOR mining colony after a deadly outbreak ravaged its fleet. Many of these “plague ships” were marked for containment.

One particular ship appears to be the chosen nesting ground of a stray Acanti, but Nova Corps has not tried to capture the massive beast. The wreckage has been marked off-limits. Clearly some sort of explosion ripped it apart from the inside, but the residual radiation is unlike anything on record. Unwilling to risk the heath of Nova Corpsman, the Worldmind decided to seal the vessel inside a nano-resin tomb with the rest of the debris.
The Quarantine Zone is a massive graveya:
The Quarantine Zone is a massive graveyard of Galactic War debris, including wrecked vessels, giant robots, explosives, and biological weapons. With no safe way to dispose of all this dangerous cargo, Nova Corps agreed to seal it all away in a protective sphere. The contents inside are bound together with an aggressive ebrium-based nano-resin cluster-foam. The foam will continue to expand and adhere to any surface, pulling all of the scrap together and eventually filling the sphere entirely. The process is currently ongoing, with new wreckage still hauled to the Quarantine Zone and added to the pile.

Until the task is complete, the Nova Corps frigate, Hala’s Hope, continues to patrol the area to make sure any contraband stays out of the hands of would-be thieves.
Halfworld is a planet in the Keystone Qu:
Halfworld is a planet in the Keystone Quadrant spilt almost directly in half, with one side covered in lush forest and the other completely industrialized. As an important asset of the Kree Empire, Halfworld was expected to bolster its military might with experimental weapon projects. Primarily focusing on AI and robotics, such as the massive Kree Sentries, they soon realized they had a valuable, unexploited resource—animals living deep in the woods. Thus, the Kree hybrid program began.

Abducted animals found themselves altered by bioengineering—their brains augmented with A.I. and their bodies physically enhanced. A rare few even gained sentience, which created several violent incidents and at least one reported escape. The hybrids did go on to fight in the Galactic War and most of them were sacrificed as acceptable losses while creating distractions or holding the line just a bit longer for the Kree soldiers to survive. Halfworld has gone silent since the war and it is unclear whether the experiments continue.
Katath is a remote planet known for its:
Katath is a remote planet known for its harsh climate and harsher people. One might mistake it for a primitive world due to its tribal society and a heavy focus on hunting and agriculture. However, Katathians are perfectly evolved for their environment. A vast majority of the population is in peak physical condition, including the elderly. In fact, Katathians are often welcomed into off-world crews due to their hardiness and survival prowess, as well as their strict code of honor.

Though somewhat new to interstellar travel, the Katathians can hold their own against superior fleets, credited mainly to their fearless captains and brute force attacks. Thanos used these traits against them during the Galactic War, diverting their defense and then razing a large portion of Katath. The Katathians are rebuilding faster than most other races, as expected, but the damage to their morale will linger for generations to come.
Lady Hellbender’s fortress on Seknarf Ni:
Lady Hellbender’s fortress on Seknarf Nine serves many important functions. It is the grand palace of the world’s unquestioned ruler, an awesome display of her power, a center for monster-traders and diplomats to barter with the Monster Queen, a barracks and hangar for her impressive army, and, perhaps most importantly, a pen for breeding and caring for her extensive collection of terrible beasts.

The fortress was originally a religious temple built by Seknarf Nine’s oppressive ruling priests and was designed to worship their monster gods. Many lives were taken within these walls, both from cycles and cycles of sacrifice and the bloody slaughter of the priests themselves when Lady Hellbender rose against them.
Built into the side of a large asteroid:
Built into the side of a large asteroid in the Tayo system, the Rock is a primary Nova Corps station tasked with overseeing all peacekeeping operations for a dozen sectors. It is a deep space extension of New Xandar, allowing consultation and diplomacy with the Worldmind as well as serving as a dispatch for Nova Corps operations. Thousands of Nova Corps workers live within the Rock and help to maintain the station, oversee more business-related tasks, and provide law enforcement.

After the Galactic War left Nova Corps in ruins, reconstruction efforts focused simultaneously on New Xandar and the Rock. The Worldmind believed that the Corps could not remain on the defensive, but would need to extend their presence back into the galaxy at large.
The last spaceport on the edge of the kn:
The last spaceport on the edge of the known universe, Knowhere drifts precariously along the edge of the Rift.

Long before it was a bustling city, it was a nameless research station built inside the gigantic, severed head of one of the godlike Celestials. Research quickly turned to profit as various illegal mining operations set up to harvest the potent brain matter. The commercial side of Knowhere sprang up to feed and service the researchers-turned-miners. Food supplies became a plethora of market kiosks, offering cuisine from every corner of the galaxy. Shelters became brothels and bars. Many soon traded their mining tools for untraceable firearms as they moved towards back-alley deals, assassination contracts, and smuggling operations.
  
The station’s head of security, Cosmo, maintains a loose kind of order, keeping the various criminal factions from tearing the place apart, while allowing them their questionable operations so business can continue. Knowhere sits outside the jurisdiction of Nova Corps and remains neutral in galactic conflicts.
Unless you’re in the market for criminal:
Unless you’re in the market for criminal contracts or looking for goons, it is ill-advised to have a drink in Mantlo’s Bar. This watering hole for Knowhere’s shadiest denizens has a nasty reputation, and not just for its low hygiene standards—many of the galaxy’s biggest heists, abductions, and assassinations have been plotted between these grimy walls. Mantlo’s is a place where even the bartender can be trusted to sell a secret. Once seated inside the bar, a patron is assumed to be buying or selling something illegal.

Knowhere Chief of Security Cosmo turns a blind eye to Mantlo’s, as part of an agreement with the criminal element to keep the peace, but many suspect he’s listening in telepathically for any direct threats to the station.
The Rift, sometimes called “The Rip” by:
The Rift, sometimes called “The Rip” by locals, is the end of the universe. Scientists believe that all matter, time, and reality itself disintegrates as it is slowly pulled into the hungry maw. Others believe it is a wormhole into another timeline, or even a galaxy with completely alien physics, but any exploratory technology sent into the Rift is pulverized upon approach. Some religions have proposed that it’s a gateway into eternal punishment for a sinful life or a great drain opened to erase a failed galactic experiment, so that the gods can begin anew.

Pilgrims from across the galaxy have made their way to Knowhere to gaze into this menacing abyss, this anti-creation. The harrowing experience has led to countless holy books and modified prophecies. Many of Knowhere’s laborers gather before it each morning, pondering their own mortality before heading to work.
Rumors travel fast on the Knowhere stati:
Rumors travel fast on the Knowhere station. Speculation about the dead Celestial’s remaining power is an old tradition. Whispers suggest that the brain stem has been reactivated to allow travel through space, dimensions, and perhaps even time itself. However, control of the Cortex is strictly protected by the station’s security chief, Cosmo, and his loyal pack of security guards. 

Everybody’s heard from a friend of a friend who claims to have traveled through the Cortex, supposedly riding an enormous five-fingered hand made of pure energy. Some stories speak of quick glimpses of various alternate timelines along the way. Others suggest these are just hallucinations caused by the extreme mental stress of hurling one’s particles through space. Cosmo refuses to discuss the matter.
Sacrosanct is assumed to be the current:
Sacrosanct is assumed to be the current capital ship for the Universal Church of Truth, recently making its presence known again after the cult’s presumed collapse. As a former DSOR (Deep Space Ore Requisition) mining vessel, it is sized to house and support an entire colony while also facilitating the drilling, collection, and storage of large amounts of ore. It is also equipped with a full array of defense turrets to ward off potential pirates, especially the more technologically adept Ravagers.

It is unknown what modifications the colonists have made to the interior of this vessel since their conversion to the Church, but a few comm-vids with its agents have confirmed a more decorative, religious theme. Diplomats have not yet been welcomed aboard Sacrosanct.
Under the watchful eye of the Xandarian:
Under the watchful eye of the Xandarian Worldmind and their Nova Corps police force, the thriving world of Xandar was completely decimated by a Chitauri surprise attack that would mark the start of the Galactic War. Only one Nova Corps squadron survived, led by a human centurion named Richard Rider. Rider teamed up with the Worldmind to cobble together a successful Resistance movement. Once the war ended, many Resistance fighters returned to the Xandarian home world to help the Worldmind rebuild.

Now home to the remaining Xandarians, the thriving metropolis called New Xandar is a technological wonder, a gargantuan space station metropolis drifting near the remains of their shattered world. The civilians attempt to recapture their former lives in extensive residential areas while a large portion of the station is dedicated to rebuilding Nova Corps and projecting an image of strength across the galaxy.
Everything about this remote planet is a:
Everything about this remote planet is an enigma. While its surface is largely covered by starkly contrasting dunes and oceans, its center appears to be a series of hollowed-out tunnels. In fact, researchers have found no evidence of a traditional solid or liquid planetary core, which should be physically impossible. Yet Lamentis remains hospitable to life. 

Its largest village, Nok Tamal, houses both the Priests of Pama and, under their care, the remnants of the Cotati civilization. Here, the priests continue their meditations on peace and prophecy, far enough from any spaceport to not be bothered by the galaxy’s perpetual chaos. With Cotati assistance, the priests are in-tune with local flora and fauna, running Nok Tamal in perfect harmony with the bizarre natural world around it.
Scans of the winding cave system beneath:
Scans of the winding cave system beneath Lamentis’ surface reveal a scientific impossibility: they appear to weave their way entirely through the core of the planet. The conundrum has attracted the attention of many researchers, but the Cotati who guard the caves forbid visitors. The only existing accounts of the tunnels come from the Priests of Pama during their initial exploration. However, their journals are of little help since the writings are generally cryptic and focused on prophecy rather than geology.

The priests do note some evidence of an ancient civilization in the caves, but they do not elaborate. If one ignores the wilder, more mythical warnings about the caves, there are enough descriptions of Lamentis’ various cave predators to discourage trespass.
Maklu IV is a deep-frozen planet with en:
Maklu IV is a deep-frozen planet with enough deadly weather to keep all but the bravest travelers away. If the frigid winds do not kill you, perhaps the asteroid belt forever raining fire upon Maklu’s surface will do the trick. Or maybe the extremely lethal venomous plants? Recent reports also mention that flesh-eating ape men have entered the food chain, somewhere in the middle tiers. The planet’s rumored apex predator is none other than Fin Fang Foom, a legendary Kakarantharan dragon.

With the destruction wrought by the Galactic War, Maklu IV became a popular destination for Katathian pilgrims, seeking to hunt its great beasts to die with purpose and honor. Their hunt markers litter the planet, now serving as tombstones.
Little is known about the core section o:
Little is known about the core section of Sacrosanct, which was originally engineered to secure, mine, and process massive ore samples, allowing crews to work from inside the rock. Since its miners converted to the Universal Church of Truth, no one has been permitted inside without a certain rank in the organization. Though external scans are spotty, one thing is clear: The Church discovered a new source of energy and experienced a massive technology boom. Traces of the old mining equipment remain, but they are augmented by unknown machinery. Certain areas have been hollowed out but emit such strong radiation that they cannot be scanned.

There are a few accounts from former Church members who call this rock structure the “Cradle.” The question remains—what are they nurturing inside?

Originally built by Gene and Molly Quill: Originally built by Gene and Molly Quill, this humble Earth farm in St. Charles, Missouri, produced and sold grain to the local community. It was inherited by their daughter, Meredith, who raised her son, Peter, on the property. While the family lived a relatively simple life, neighbors reported two separate incidents of unusual disturbances such as loud noises and bright lights. In a police report of the first occurrence, Meredith confessed to holding a large rock music party in the back field. The hundreds of reports of the second occurrence have all been heavily redacted and reveal no details.
Formerly a fighter in the Ravager’s pira:
Formerly a fighter in the Ravager’s pirate fleet, the Milano has seen her share of combat and has been impounded numerous times for various charges. She’s a warp-capable M-Class ship, with impressive scouting speed and a modified arsenal capable of downing much larger vessels. Nova Corps records show the Milano’s involvement in the Galactic War, though the details have mostly been redacted. During those cycles, her repair records had listed her irreparably damaged on three different occasions. Apparently, her pilot refuses to give up on her. Updated records have registered the Milano to the Gardeners of the Galaxy.

All Ravager vessels follow the same designation pattern—naming the vessel after a wife or lover. We can assume the Milano is named for the current pilot’s past love interest. Who was this “Milano?” Was she a pirate as well?
When a Guardian is incapacitated, approa: When a Guardian is incapacitated, approach them and hold to help get them back in the fight. They will also recover on their own, but more slowly.
Calls-to-Action are short windows of opp: Calls-to-Action are short windows of opportunity that may appear during combat against certain enemies. When conditions are met, the prompt appears briefly above the enemy. Pressing before the prompt disappears inspires a Guardian to perform a special attack that permanently hinders the enemy, making them easier to defeat.
Health Markers are small, diamond-shaped:
Health Markers are small, diamond-shaped icons at the top of an enemy's Health Display.

They represent additional Health. Enemies cannot be defeated until the markers are destroyed and the final Health Bar emptied.
Thanos taught us that our own bodies are:
Thanos taught us that our own bodies are our most reliable weapons. Disarmed or captured, my sister and I remained just as lethal. This suit was custom-designed to enhance my natural movements. Armor where I'm vulnerable. Ridges and blades where I connect. Easy cleanup.
