Everything about this remote planet is a:
Everything about this remote planet is an enigma. While its surface is largely covered by starkly contrasting dunes and oceans, its center appears to be a series of hollowed-out tunnels. In fact, researchers have found no evidence of a traditional solid or liquid planetary core, which should be physically impossible. Yet Lamentis remains hospitable to life. 

Its largest village, Nok Tamal, houses both the Priests of Pama and, under their care, the remnants of the Cotati civilization. Here, the priests continue their meditations on peace and prophecy, far enough from any spaceport to not be bothered by the galaxy’s perpetual chaos. With Cotati assistance, the priests are in-tune with local flora and fauna, running Nok Tamal in perfect harmony with the bizarre natural world around it.
The Galactic War was an armed conflict t:
The Galactic War was an armed conflict that claimed the lives of trillions of sentient beings. The aggressors were the Chitauri, a warlike race bent on conquest to expand their territory. Thanos the Mad Titan allied with them, focusing their attacks on their enemy’s key seats of power. Together, they destroyed Xandar, host world of Nova Corps. The Chitauri sliced the planet into pieces. Kree-Lar, capital city-state of the Kree, was the next to fall.

But the Chitauri underestimated the resiliency and determination of their opponents. The Kree army regrouped, bolstering their forces with “The Resistance,” a ragtag fleet of fighters who’d been harassing Chitauri warships since Xandar’s destruction. Eventually, the Kree and Resistance fleets launched a three-pronged attack on Chitauri Prime. Each attacked on a different front while a stealth group of skilled operatives landed and captured the Chitauri infant queen. The Chitauri quickly surrendered. Thanos himself was ultimately slain by a vengeful Katathian named Drax the Destroyer. 

Cycles later, the impact of the war can still be felt across the galaxy as people try to pick up the pieces and rebuild.
The unmistakable silhouette of a Ravager:
The unmistakable silhouette of a Ravager ship was once enough to panic any merchant vessel. The Ravagers were a collection of motley crews, banded together under one pirate banner. They were the reason most interstellar cargo ships now travel with advanced weaponry or security escorts. Nova Corps tried many times to crack down on them, but their arrests were often jailbroken by the substantial pirate fleet. Many of the most wanted were shielded by the galaxy’s various crime lords.

Their reign of terror stopped with the arrest of their “untouchable” leader, Yondu Udonta. Purportedly ratted out by one of his own crew, Udonta was arrested by Nova Corps and sentenced to life imprisonment in the Kyln. The betrayal spread distrust and doubt throughout the Ravagers, causing division. They have yet to reunite under a new leader, but Nova Corps warns that they are still a major threat waiting to once again reveal itself.
The Chitauri are a hate-filled race of s:
The Chitauri are a hate-filled race of shapeshifters and evolutionary offshoots of the Skrull. They believe their existential purpose is to expand their empire through the destruction or subjugation of all life in the universe. This doctrine led them into launching the Galactic War. They nearly conquered everything until the combined forces of the Kree Empire and the Resistance  fleet pushed them back to Chitauri Prime and put their infant queen at risk. Unable to function without their monarch, the Chitauri surrendered.

Now they are a broken people. They are forbidden spacefaring vessels and any technology that could be considered weaponry. Under close watch by a council of united planets, Chitauri Prime has become a prison world. However, those who have faced them in battle know that they are insidious schemers and infiltrators. Many worry that they are already plotting their revenge.
Known for exceptional arrogance, the Kre:
Known for exceptional arrogance, the Kree are an advanced militaristic race from the planet Hala who obsess over genetic purity. The Kree control over a thousand worlds, many of which have become centers for biomechanical engineering and genetic manipulation. They are eager to push the limits of evolution and, on some worlds, have even divided their society into castes based on blue or pink skin. 

The Kree are ruled by the Supreme Intelligence, which, similar to the Xandarian Worldmind, is an amalgamation of minds, processed and compiled from deceased Kree. Though the Kree can be difficult to tolerate, they’ve found their place among various populations across the galaxy and boast some of the most renowned Galactic War heroes.
Nova Corps is an interstellar peacekeepi:
Nova Corps is an interstellar peacekeeping militia commanded by the collective intelligence of the Xandarian Worldmind. Through the Worldmind, Nova Corpsmen can use the power of the Nova Force to wield impressive weaponry and travel through space. Though never granted authority by the countless worlds under their watch, Nova Corps is mostly accepted as a galactic defense force, especially during large scale conflicts. 

Nova Corps was nearly wiped out at the start of the Galactic War, when the Chitauri attacked Xandar and the Corps sacrificed themselves to allow evacuation. Now in the process of rebuilding and restoring galactic order, the Corps finds itself stretched thin and vulnerable, something the Worldmind will not admit. Criminal elements are thriving with the reduced scrutiny, but Nova Corps has recently been making examples of the ones they do catch. As New Xandar nears completion, the Nova Corps is once again a galactic force to be taken seriously.
The Spartoi Empire originated from its c:
The Spartoi Empire originated from its capital planet, Spartax, and extended to a hundred different worlds. The Spartoi were a military-focused people who valued monarchy above all else, raising the Emperor of Spartax to an almost god-like status. The entire Empire once moved at his command and, if he fell, the royal succession line was extensively charted to ensure an immediate transfer of power.

Historians believe that the Chitauri took advantage of this weakness to eliminate a serious threat before the Galactic War. They located and abducted a member of the Spartoi royal bloodline, keeping the Empire inert long enough to deploy their own fleet, destroying all communications and military capabilities.

Spartax has not restored interplanetary communications since the Galactic War, leaving the rest of its former empire in the dark. Where they once produced and openly sold some of the most advanced weapons technology known to the galaxy, they have now completely isolated themselves. All diplomatic missions have failed.
The Chitauri began their wave of slaught:
The Chitauri began their wave of slaughter at the start of the Galactic War by destroying the Nova Corps host world, Xandar. With Nova Corps nearly eradicated, the galaxy was left without its primary peace-keeping force. Only one small squadron of Nova Centurions remained, led by Richard Rider. The Xandarian Worldmind tried to recall them, determined to protect their repository of Xandarian history and culture. But Rider defied them and assembled a Resistance force to take the fight right to the Chitauri.

With the Worldmind loudly protesting inside his helmet, Rider’s Resistance toured the bombed worlds and promised justice to their broken people. With every stop, his forces grew. The Resistance fleet became a parade of various races and ships all flying the same flag – a Nova Corps symbol surrounded by flames. Little by little, they took back worlds, destroying Chitauri raiders along the way. Rider’s entourage soon included most of the Katathian defense force, the Centaurian Shadows, the Rigellian Thinker Fleet, and even Gamora Zen-Whoberi, daughter of Thanos.
Lady Hellbender's Hellraisers of Seknarf:
Lady Hellbender's Hellraisers of Seknarf Nine serve as both royal guards and elite soldiers as they protect the Monster Queen and her menagerie of rare and terrible beasts. They are trained extensively to properly herd and care for the many deadly predators that often roam freely in their presence, but the job has a disturbingly high rate of accidents.

Despite intimidating uniforms meant to evoke the raw ferocity of their mistress’ monsters, it’s well known that the Hellraisers are more than eager to put down their weapons and spend an evening of drinks and debauchery with successful monster sellers. In fact, they are known to do this every night. Lady Hellbender gives them leeway, knowing that any guard who loses their edge will simply become food for her “children.”
A bizarre phenomenon is sweeping through:
A bizarre phenomenon is sweeping through the galaxy, leaving previously rational people changed in a profound way. Scientists from several worlds have pooled their expertise to find a cause and a potential cure, but they have had little success. Experts cannot even agree on whether it is a virus, some type of brainwashing, or perhaps something less scientific and more in the realm of mystics. They have, however, compiled a list of observations about these “Converted.”

Most distinguishable is a sickly purple glow, or aura, around the body. The energy generated is currently unidentified and impossible to measure. The minds of the Converted are altered and though they appear to retain much of their former selves, they are driven to coordinate with other Converted. Any former goals are replaced by a need to spread the message about something they call “The Promise,” which seems to be their version of paradise for all sentient creatures. Do not mistake this for pacifism. While the Converted appear calm and collected, they will attack with extreme violence if their message is rejected.

The delivery method for this malady remains a mystery, but it is spreading fast. Nova Corps has advised isolation and quarantine until more is known.
When Cosmo took command of Knowhere, a h:
When Cosmo took command of Knowhere, a haven for the galaxy's worst criminals, his primary goal was keeping the peace. He knew he'd need a reliable, incorruptible security force to help him do it. The perfect candidates arrived in the form of the Korbinites.

With their planet eaten by Galactus, the World-Devourer, the Korbinite survivors fled across the galaxy, eventually docking their sentient ship at Knowhere. Cosmo probed their minds telepathically to reveal their intent, finding them to be peaceful and eager to fit into a chaotic new world. As a hardy people with a strong sense of justice, they were a perfect match.
The Universal Church of Truth is a techn:
The Universal Church of Truth is a techno-religious organization focused on healing and the relief of suffering. It began after its founded members, deep space miners, lost most of their colony to an incurable disease. The group grew during the Galactic War as world after world fell to the Chitauri assault. Reports of a holy man, an actual healer, traveling with the Church only drew more of the weary and wounded. Led by the “Grand Unifier,” Raker, the Church brought rising hope in a time of great loss.

However, the Church started to buckle under the weight of war casualties and the death of its healer “god.” By the war’s end, they had all but disappeared. The Church has since resurfaced with the Grand Unifier once again at the forefront, but Nova Corps has registered it as a minor sect without significant influence.
The Lethal Legion is a band of super-pow:
The Lethal Legion is a band of super-powered mercenaries operating from Knowhere’s eclectic spaceport. They are led by Glah-ree, a disgraced Kree soldier who now calls himself Captain Glory. Eager to claim the highest paying contracts and conquer the most intimidating challenges, the Lethal Legion takes on high-profile bounty-hunting jobs that most would deem suicidal. As a result, the roster is constantly in flux as its members are frequently killed off. The seemingly invincible twins calling themselves “The Blood Brothers” maintain their spot on the team, but former members include many notorious criminals, including Metal Master, Mentacle, Drall, and Ferene. 

As of late, the Lethal Legion has been working jobs primarily for the Monster Queen of Seknarf Nine.
The Cotati are highly intelligent plantl:
The Cotati are highly intelligent plantlike beings, originally from Hala, who taught their psychic talents to a small sect of Kree pacifist priests. This angered the Kree Supreme Intelligence, who then banished the priests and ordered the Cotati’s extermination. The fallen Cotati left seeds behind for the priests to gather and bring to a new world, a remote planet called Lamentis. There, the Cotati were carefully planted and nursed until their race was born anew.

The two groups founded their own sanctuary, a village they named Nok Tamal. There, the Cotati guard the secrets of Lamentis’ ancient cave system as they continue to explore the full potential of their minds.
Originally from Hala, the Priests of Pam:
Originally from Hala, the Priests of Pama are a sect of Kree pacifists who found themselves persecuted by their own kind. To defend themselves, they studied forbidden martial arts and mystic meditation rituals, sharpening both mind and body. This drew the attention of another Halasian race in hiding--the plantlike Cotati. The Cotati offered to teach their new friends how to hone their psychic abilities in exchange for protection. The Kree Supreme Intelligence discovered their alliance and banished both groups. It was a bloody exodus.

The Priests of Pama now manage a Cotati refuge on Lamentis, where they nurture and protect the endangered plant race. The Priests believe that the Cotati, as well as Mantis, their “Celestial Madonna,” will eventually produce a Celestial Messiah who will usher in peace to the entire galaxy.
Voxiplodes were created in a Rigellian b:
Voxiplodes were created in a Rigellian bioweapon lab as an efficient way to disable an enemy ship from the inside. A hull-breaching bore-missile delivered the payload and unleashed havoc upon the unsuspecting crew.

The voxiplode’s method of locomotion is extremely simple: dropping and rolling along its gelatinous, thorny surface. It has an eye on each of its faces used to locate enemy life forms, but also to spot and coordinate with others of its kind. A voxiplode swarm is capable of significant damage. Its deadliest trait, however, is its ability to reform into more voxiplodes if it is torn into pieces, adding more numbers to its horde.

The Rigellians underestimated the resilience of their creatures, causing significant post-war complications after the Galactic War ended and cleanup began.
These unusual creatures are found exclus:
These unusual creatures are found exclusively in Nova Corps’ post-war wreckage dump, the Quarantine Zone. The fact that they were never seen before led scientists to believe it was a mutation caused by the radiation and toxic substances within the crashed ships. Genetic analysis concluded that the moniscobule was originally a Huskian spindlerat, a common breed of vermin found aboard many deep spaceships. This mutation has increased its size tenfold and distorted its body to the point where it is unrecognizable.

Nova Corps has assured scientists that these unfortunate beasts will be sealed away and destroyed with the rest of the hazardous contents of the Quarantine Zone bubble.
The shollock is a nasty creature from Ch:
The shollock is a nasty creature from Chitauri Prime that is often used as an interrogation tool. Its original name, “chaa lloghk” translates roughly to “screaming chair,” but not for any sound the creature makes. Captured Resistance soldiers during the Galactic War feared being “shollocked” by the enemy, and for good reason. The Chitauri appear to have bred these beasts to have larger spikes and sharper edges than nature intended.

Normally kept secure in the belly of a Chitauri vessel, many shollocks were set loose upon the enemy if the ship was about to be lost to a boarding party.
Wuruums are one of the most adaptive spe:
Wuruums are one of the most adaptive species in the galaxy and it’s not unusual to find them on any planet bearing life. They’re known to plant their larvae in anything, especially fruits and vegetables, later infesting the creatures that eat them. Xenobiologists believe the booming animal trade market has almost single-handedly seeded these creatures onto multiple worlds. Without host plants to support their young, they are also capable of producing large masses of eggs. Crews fighting in the Galactic War reported waking up to find whole ship chambers covered in egg structures.

The basic wuruum has an impressive mass and uses its body to whip and crush its prey, intending to prevent escape by breaking bones. It is also capable of a thick slime spray, which weighs down and binds anything trying to escape.
Legends about the Acanti say that these:
Legends about the Acanti say that these giant space whales are spiritual knowledge-seekers who travel the cosmos in search of ancient wisdom and then, upon their impending deaths, hurl themselves into stars so that their souls may pass onto the next Acanti.

These tales certainly do not match the Acanti living on Seknarf Nine under the care of the Monster Queen. But Lady Hellbender has an explanation. She claims her Acanti are rescues, taken from the Brood, who wanted to use them as spacefaring vessels. Her whales had been lobotomized, robbed of their free will. She has returned what she could to them. They fly free and are welcome to leave, should they again seek the stars. Instead, they remain near their savior. Oddly, these creatures known for their peaceful nature fight vigorously to protect their Queen.
These deceptively slow-moving gelatinous:
These deceptively slow-moving gelatinous cubes often surprise their prey by hurling themselves forward or ambushing from above. The strange biology of a Seknarfian jackogel consists of a living crystal core surrounded by a protective/digestive barrier of slime. 

Xenobiologist Fer-Gom has run several extensive experiments to measure the creature’s intelligence, but she concluded that they don’t actually think outside of four basic commands: “see food, move towards food, kill food, eat food.”

Fer-Gom updated her list upon discovering more evolved jackogels deep in the Seknarfian wilds. It now includes “shred food with crystal spikes,” and “explode.”
Mantane are airborne predatory beasts th:
Mantane are airborne predatory beasts that were nearly hunted to extinction for their pliable hides and the delicious egg clusters they carry upon their backs. Mantane caviar is one of the most frequently smuggled goods in the galaxy. However, they are not easy prey. What would appear to be fangs near the front of their skulls are venomous stingers, unrelated to their mouths. A deep sting from the female of this species causes excruciating pain, if not death. The male’s sting causes mild irritation. Unfortunately, there is no way to identify which is which without a lab analysis, since all mantane produce and carry eggs.

The mantane are thriving once again on Seknarf Nine thanks to the Monster Queen’s preservation efforts.
Slakebeasts can be found throughout the:
Slakebeasts can be found throughout the wilds of Seknarf Nine. They are extremely fast, sleek quadrupeds with fang-filled, splayed faces. Although they rely heavily on scent to hunt, they do have a set of rudimentary eyes within their mouth structures. An aggressive slakebeast might “roar” to get a better look at its victim. Its bite is deadly, but its tail is an even bigger cause for concern. Slakebeasts have evolved the ability to freeze prey with a glowing barb, a skill they use to trap their primary food source—the jackogel.

But on a monster planet like Seknarf Nine, even the fearsome slakebeast sits low on the food chain. They are a frequent meal for Lady Hellbender’s much larger monsters.
The Seknarfian common barbwing wears its:
The Seknarfian common barbwing wears its entire digestive system on the outside. Its stomach extends along the entire length of its underbelly and is covered in tiny, fanged feeding-sphincters. Using its taloned wings and its impressive pinchers, it traps its prey, wrapping its entire body around the other animal to eat.

Because it seeks exposed flesh, it is typical for a barbwing to target a person’s face and neck. Seknarfian locals know that when they encounter an attack of this nature, it’s often more humane to just shoot the victim.
The K'aian warthos is a towering quadrup:
The K'aian warthos is a towering quadruped capable of carrying fifty times its own weight, making it an exceptional beast of burden. It has enormous tusks it uses to burrow into the sides of rocky cliffs. When K'aians hear this thunderous sound, they immediately rally their defenses. A warthos protecting its den can easily tear down an entire village.

The Monster Queen of Seknarf Nine owns nearly as many warthos as there are on K'ai. She has used them to reconstruct her palace, transport goods, and as the backbone of her personal monster army. She treats her beasts so well, they pose no threat to her property.
The tara-tara is an odd little creature:
The tara-tara is an odd little creature from Maklu IV that looks like a pile of eyeballs bursting out of a tiny frame. However, it can convincingly mimic just about any living creature it sees, even shrinking or enlarging its mass to pull off the deception. Its meek appearance is another trick, as it will often lure in a much larger beast looking for an easy meal and then transform into something even bigger.

Though the tara-tara appears to be of average animal intelligence, its camouflage is not just visual. It imitates scent and even behavior so expertly that another beast’s own family cannot tell the difference. As such a dangerous and entertaining evolutionary oddity, the tara-tara remains in high demand by monster collectors.
Skrats can be found throughout Knowhere,:
Skrats can be found throughout Knowhere, but the largest packs of them inhabit the market. These tiny balls of fur are incredibly fast and weigh very little. In fact, a skrat is in no danger of falling from one of Knowhere’s many precarious walkways since they’ll gently float down to safety. Knowhere skratcatchers have very little luck apprehending the vermin due to their exceptional vision and multiple eyes.

While skrats originally survived by stealing food from Knowhere’s miners, they have since thrived on the market’s garbage and dropped crumbs. Their population has grown exponentially over the past few cycles, which has led the station’s chief of security, Cosmo, to begin chasing them down himself.
Formerly known as 28-T Deep Dredgers, th:
Formerly known as 28-T Deep Dredgers, the “Inquisitor” machines of the Universal Church of Truth were once deep space mining robots. When the mining ships cored out a large ore sample, the colony would begin to construct their workstations inside. These robots would begin the initial work to ensure the environment was safe enough to move in construction crews.

The robots have since been heavily modified to serve as personal Guards for Grand Unifier Raker. With new hardware and powered by an unquantifiable energy source, “faith,” the Inquisitor’s abilities cannot be measured. However, one can assume their previous functions do remain. They have solid, flexible metal bodies and can extend their limbs great distances. Specialized tools that enable them to quickly drill through rock and project cutting lasers make them a formidable foe.
The Otroogi is one of Seknarf Nine’s lar:
The Otroogi is one of Seknarf Nine’s largest beasts, capable of growing as tall as the treeline itself. Unfortunately, the former ruler-priests slaughtered the largest of the herd to build ritual structures with their gargantuan bones. The fiercely protected otroogi that remain on the planet are adolescents and will not reach their full size for thousands of rotations.

The Otroogi uses its sturdy shoulder blades to pinch and clip the tallest branches, depositing various fruits onto its flat back. Its prehensile tubes reach up, sort through its food, and then deliver it to its mouth. The flat horn on an otroogi’s skull and its deadly claws are used exclusively for defense. It is a herbivore.
The Priests of Pama have described Lamen:
The Priests of Pama have described Lamentis’ “Languishing Fog” in mystical terms, which is not particularly useful for xenobiologists. They say it is alive and that it follows them as they travel the tunnels below the surface. They also claim it seeps into the mind and exposes one’s inner turmoil or awakens one’s inner eyes.

But they seem to be hiding something more sinister. Off-worlders have met with some of the priests who have encountered this fog and found them to be in a near-vegetative state, barely able to utter words and unable to care for themselves. One cotati warned visitors that the fog was a psychic parasite before the priests silenced him.

Is this mysterious vapor a toxic hallucinogen? If it stalks its prey like the priests have described, then surely it is alive.
These hulking cave dwellers are found de:
These hulking cave dwellers are found deep in the tunnels of Lamentis. They may have once been a more advanced race, perhaps even the sculptors behind the many bizarre statues down in the depths. However, they are now in complete symbiosis with a diverse combination of cave plants and fungi. Unfortunately for the host creatures, one particular type of fungus has replaced most of the brain tissue needed for higher functions and driven them towards more primal needs. It appears the fungus prefers the dark, since none of these beasts has been observed on the planet’s surface. 

The Priests of Pama have tried to communicate with the ogrode but have only been met with violence so far.
The avalog is a Makluvian predator that:
The avalog is a Makluvian predator that spends cycles asleep beneath the planet’s extensive ice plains. They only come to the surface after significant meteorite fall, presumably to prey upon the traumatized surface creatures. An avalog will drag its kills back down with it, so it’s common to find half-eaten carcasses below layers of solid ice. 

It has four powerful tentacles for defense and locomotion and two highly-sensitive feelers capable of detecting subtle vibrations through Maklu IV’s frozen lakes. As one Makluvian explorer reported, “its head is 250% teeth.”
The Makluvian mushiiger is a vile beast:
The Makluvian mushiiger is a vile beast covered in venomous pustules, a natural defense system to keep the planet’s many mega-predators from eating it. Its prime defensive tool becomes a weapon as it seeks to spray its victims with the same venom, melting down the flesh for easier consumption. 

Due to the amount of fluids near the surface of its skin, the mushiiger must expend an exceptional amount of energy to keep from freezing. Although not apparent to the naked eye, the beast is constantly shivering with such controlled, tiny movements that it stays warm. As a result, it is perpetually hungry.
The Wendigo may seem perfectly suited fo:
The Wendigo may seem perfectly suited for Maklu IV’s frigid climate, but they’re a recent, chaotic addition to the planet’s ecosystem. The beasts are thought to be Terran, likely brought aboard one of the many crashed ships that dot the planet’s surface. The Wendigo have grown in numbers rapidly, seemingly reproducing through a transformational bite. Nova Corps recently interviewed a captured poacher who claims his entire crew was ambushed, bitten, and transformed overnight. They now wander the frozen forests as Wendigo themselves, driven by a need to consume the flesh of other humanoids.

The beasts are massive, bipedal creatures covered in shaggy white fur with a maw full of serrating fangs, razor-sharp claws, and a long tail for balance as they stalk high above in the frozen trees. They are capable of surprisingly silent movement, although they often announce their presence by screaming out a single word—WENDIGO.

It’s unknown how the expanding Wendigo tribe will fair against Maklu’s awesome predators, but at the rate they are multiplying, they may soon have the numbers to stand a chance.
The Makluvian breed of wuruum has adapte: The Makluvian breed of wuruum has adapted to extreme cold and is able to burrow and nest inside thick walls of ice. In fact, it has become so in-tune with its habitat that its hunting techniques have changed to match the frigid temperatures. It has evolved to spit a rapidly-freezing mucus at its prey, locking its victim in place so it can feed itself or seed its young. As one of the smaller beasts on a planet filled with gargantuan predators, the ice wuruum strikes only when it has an advantage in numbers or position and makes quick work of the carcass before retreating into its hole.
Centurion Ker-Darr has lost his arm to t:
Centurion Ker-Darr has lost his arm to the nano-resin, though accounts of this accident contradict each other. Ker-Darr maintains that the nano-resin “splashed” him, instantly encasing him up to his elbow. However, his Corpsmen have reported that he put his arm inside on a dare, directly violating safety measures and, of course, costing him said limb. The acidic compounds within the resin are designed to break down space-worthy metals, so we were not surprised to find it dissolving his arm within the span of a few micro-cycles.

My recommendation: a refresher course on safety protocols within the Quarantine Zone and a stern warning about pranks or bets during any Nova Corps mission. I do not advise punishment for Centurion Ker-Darr because his synthetic arm will serve as a constant reminder of his folly, no matter which story is true.
After the Chitauri destroyed our outpost:
After the Chitauri destroyed our outpost, we journeyed for 15 rotations to reach the Healer. Every night was harder than the next as Jxllem’s breathing worsened. We could find nothing medically wrong with him – the Chitauri assault had damaged his mind and he was simply… giving up. After he’d led us through so many battles, we weren’t about to let him go out this way. 

We found His Church aboard one of its converted mining ships. The line was long, but the excitement was palpable. Each time we advanced, we would hear screams of joy at the front of the crowd. When it was our turn, we approached this gold-skinned miracle worker. I do not have the proper vocabulary to describe him, but it is the closest we have ever been to divinity. The Healer pressed his hands against Jxllem’s forehead and whispered to him. Our friend’s eyes widened and he took a deep breath for the first time since he fell in battle. Oxxo be praised, he was healed! 

Jxllem has been… distant on our return trip, we believe he is simply dealing with his near-death experience. We hope he will be himself once again soon.
My heart, do not come back to Hala. Ther:
My heart, do not come back to Hala. There is nothing here for you. I fear it will soon fall as so many other worlds have. Kree-Lar is in flames. Most of the spaceports have been decimated. The Chitauri have gathered many of our remaining leaders and have announced public executions. Fear not, we escaped—we are on a Shi’ar mercy ship and headed for refuge. Those monsters are focused on destroying our cities. So far, they are not pursuing us. We will survive this, even if our beautiful Hala does not.

Continue your work on Halfworld. I beg of you, demand that your leaders unleash everything they have to make these monsters suffer. Every unfinished machine. Every experimental weapon. All of it. Right into the heart of Chitauri Prime. Show them the superior might of the Kree Empire! Make your children proud!
Got some real bad news for you, sis. The:
Got some real bad news for you, sis. Them critters you had me smuggle off of Crackgh II? You didn’t tell me they bred like Seknarfian mudhogs. I got a cargo bay full of the ugly flarkers and they grew up FAST. I can hear them banging on the walls and shrieking something fierce. Probably hungry. When I saw my fuel was leaking, I put two and two together and realized they’re chewing up my fuel lines. 

To make it worse, I gotta fly right through a Nova Creeps blockade. I ain’t got no way to hide them things, so I’m thinking about scuttling this old heap and taking my shuttle to Knowhere. Expect a bill for a new ship soon and we can figure out our next haul. I know you’re good for it. 

What can I say? Scut happens.
I write this report so that the efforts:
I write this report so that the efforts and the courage of my people may echo throughout time. We had finally accomplished the unthinkable—after generations of war, we put aside our differences and united to achieve our dreams. I am dictating this message from the first interstellar Beeldarian vessel, our pride, the Starborus. Everything we suspected was true—there are people out here! Countless other worlds. Some of them far more advanced and some of them struggling as we did. We were welcomed with open arms by a group calling themselves the Nova Corps.

To our horror, we learned the galaxy itself is currently at war. Beeldar is right in the path of the aggressors, a violent race called the Chitauri. We requested aid from our new allies, but their rescue force will soon be intercepted by a much larger Chitauri fleet. We have decided to rapidly burn our fuel reserves to reach the Chitauri first. In our naivete, we do not have weapons on the Starborus, but she is fast, and she is built strong. We will ram their capital ship. Perhaps we can save our new friends.

Know this—for a brief, incredible moment, Beeldar found peace. We accomplished everything we set out to do. I pray our sacrifice will make a difference in our final hour.
Lady Hellbender gives us impossible task:
Lady Hellbender gives us impossible task! Wants all crashing ships cleaned up! Does not want “Chitauri” and “Resistance” junk in her forest. But there is so much! And beasts move in! Plants tangle!

And what about bridges? Ugly, but bridges work! We take down bridges? Put them where after? Maybe we anger her. Maybe she punishes us. But who will move junk if junk-movers killed by beasts? Maybe she doesn’t think about this. Maybe she doesn’t care. Only about beasts.
That’s the genius of it, see? We’ve got:
That’s the genius of it, see? We’ve got all the monsters' DNA profiles loaded in the system. Any of the Queen’s pets get loose and into the airducts, which they love for some flarkin’ reason, when the drones find them, all that do is stun them based on the profile. Makes it easier to get them back in their cages.

Not in the system, you die. End up splattered on the walls. Simple as that.

Just make sure you keep the profiles up to date. Last thing you want is the latest getting loose and dying. Hellbender’ll flay you alive if that happens. Ask Hurunn'Ol. If you can find any bits of him willing to talk.

Add your sample to the system too, in case you ever find yourself hunting down a mistake you made.

CHAPTER 03

Ka-Lor moved his legs toward the Nexus command center, took a deep breath, and summoned the Worldmind.

“Worldmind,” he commanded demandingly. 

“Ahhh, the Golden Force,” they cooed longingly in a cold, emotionless voice. “You are supposed to be on Nova patrol.”

“Patrol your collective hearts, Worldmind. You know why I’m here,” he insisted passionately.

The Worldmind quivered with each precise syllable. “We did not think you had noticed.”

“Did you know you glow brighter when you see me?” he asked questioningly.

“We are the collective minds… and hearts… of billions, Ka-Lor. Any romance between us defies reason,” they said, sadly, but also hesitatingly, as if demanding a rebuttal. 

“Here’s my rebuttal,” Ka-Lor yelled, “I am the Golden Force! My chest burns with enough love for all Xandarians!”

“And we ARE all Xandarians. That is… reasonable.”

Ka-Lor smiled warmly inside. Another victory.
That’s it. I’ve had it. \n\nIf I’ve said:
That’s it. I’ve had it. 

If I’ve said it once, I’ve said it a quintillion times.

DO NOT JUMP IN THE KRUTACKIN’ ELEVATOR!

This is the seventh service request. Seventh! 

I’m officially sending a formal complaint to the Worldmind. Let’s see how those high-and-mighty Corpsmen like a big fat reprimand on their records.

I can’t believe I joined the Corps for this.
What does a fatally wounded wuruum and M:
What does a fatally wounded wuruum and Mantlo’s Bar on Knowhere Station have in common? Both are in the midst of a slow and painful death. 

Do not get me wrong, loyal reader. I came to Knowhere on a mission. But even I, a connoisseur of dive bars and flark-ridden watering holes, cannot be swayed to give a full skull to this garishly lit den of thievery that has the audacity to call itself a bar.

For a bar suggests that there is one by which to be rated against. If Mantlo’s has a bar, it has sunk so low into the rotting celestial grey matter that it cannot – dare I say will not – be found again.

Therefore, reader, I must caution you. Drink at your own risk, lest you, too, be consumed by the slow entropy of irrelevance. A generous 0.5 out of 5555555555jksjdnhnallllllllllllllddddddddskaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
Welcome to the end of the line. All time:
Welcome to the end of the line. All time, matter, and space will eventually find its way into the Rift and become nothing. Take a moment to stare into the abyss. Bask in how ultimately meaningless this whole "reality" experiment has been and perhaps your current troubles will disappear.

Once you've finished, be sure to purchase a ticket to the Collector's Emporium to witness more cosmic oddities!
All I know is they told us we were leavi:
All I know is they told us we were leaving the Quarantine Zone. Even though we still had rotations left out there. At first I was glad. Thought maybe we'd hit our furlough. But then it started. I don't know where it started, but it crept through the ship.

People started to change. We thought it was a virus at first. Maybe that's why we left the QZ. But it got worse. They wanted people to convert to something? We tried contacting New Xandar, but the Worldmind wouldn't answer. 

Not long after, they started killing each other.

A few of us made for the escape pods, but they were waiting, or right on our heels. They were everywhere. Some of us escaped. I said I'd stay behind. Give them a chance. 

I hear them over the comms, talking about some Matriarch. Maybe I can keep hiding, but I don't think I have much longer. Everything hurts, and I just want the hurting to stop...
Could that really be him? Not AT ALL wha:
Could that really be him? Not AT ALL what I was expecting. 

Is that good or bad?

He’s not like other adults. I mean… sort of? But he’s also kind of a big dumb kid.

He thought my art was cool! 

Do all Terrans dress like that? And if so… why?

Mom will NOT talk about him. She says I should forget we ever met.

Which is all the more reason to keep digging.

As you are all aware, the Accuser will be making her diplomatic trip to Hala’s Hope next cycle to discuss the Kree Council's involvement with reconstruction efforts. However, this is not her only business on the station. All Kree currently serving Nova Corps will be expected to meet with the Accuser at the allotted time for your interrogation.

You may be asked to provide records of family history and recent medical results – not the ones provided by Nova Corps, but by a certified Kree physician from the Purity Council list. If you have children currently living with you, they may be interviewed as well.

Failure to arrive for your appointment will not be tolerated. The Accuser will be more than willing to locate you in your place of work and escort you to an interrogation room. Do be punctual.

Ka-Lor made sure his office door was locked. He pulled the shades down on his viewport. Sat at his desk and wondered just how true this story was. The client was pretty convincing. But most liars are. Still, there was something in it.

He tapped his fingers on the case file, but didn't open it. He stood up and walked to the washbasin. Looked at himself in the mirror. Grimaced, and turned away.

She'd offered him too much money for too little a job. It didn't add up.
Something about it gnawed at him.

He hurried back to the file. Turned on the light and looked over the pages carefully. There - indented on the back of the photo. A number.

0025.

Combination maybe? Contact number? he ran out, if he hurried he might be able to tail the client, she if that led anywhere.
Silas, you silly old fool. How many time:
Silas, you silly old fool. How many times will you get taken in by charlatans? I hope you come to your senses.  The dead stay dead, that’s the one true fact of the universe. 

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Sister. I hope this communication finds you well. I have wondrous news. SHE has come. The Matriarch in all her glory. We do not need to suffer anymore! The blame we have felt since the Chitauri destroyed our home and took our parents from us – SHE CAN MAKE IT RIGHT! She can free us from our despair!

Sister. I implore you. When the time comes, YOU MUST accept her gift. Accept her Promise with an open heart and together we can rejoin our parents. We can resurrect those we lost and live together in truth, without pain, until the end of eternity.

I know you will make the right decision. 

Matriarch be blessed.

Yours,
Silas
Wish the Big Man would stop his sulking:
Wish the Big Man would stop his sulking and explore this place with me. So many nooks and crannies, like those breakfast breads we had once. At least come fight some of the beasties down here. He needs to get that golden blood flowing again. Stretch his legs, show the world what for again.  

Ain’t been the same since what happened, happened to him. Just a husk of his former shell. Can’t I say I rightly blame him. Heckuva thing to go through. 

Worst part of this place is the lousy damp everywhere.
I’m off the D’ASTING Rock!\n\nPatched up:
I’m off the D’ASTING Rock!

Patched up an impounded Badoon scout shuttle with a whole mess of space-tape, nanowire, and prayers to any god, celestial being, or galactic space hoodoo that would hear them. 

Somebody must have.

No brain parasites here, so far as I can tell. Usual aches and itches. Spent a lot of time in front of the mirror trying to decide if I was crazy.

Pretty sure I’m just old.

Docked at Knowhere. Figure this far out and so close to the Rift, it’s the safest place in the Galaxy to hide from whatever mind-goblins got inside the Corpsmen. 

One thing’s for sure—Knowhere’s never going to run out of maintenance work. Figure it’s as good a place as any to finish out my days in peace.
An investigation with Knowhere security:
An investigation with Knowhere security has been opened. An officer will be along shortly to speak with you. 

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

Is there somebody we can talk to in person? This is urgent!!!

We bought tickets to the Collector's Emporium and our son, Klid, ran ahead because he was so excited to see the stupid frog. Before we could catch up, the doors SHUT between us!

There was no announcement. Nothing! And then everything started rumbling and we panicked and backed up and then the whole museum just took off and left the station with our little boy inside! We don't know where the Collector is going or how to even contact him. This is abduction!

It doesn't even make sense! Why would the Collector kidnap Klid? There’s not even anything unique or interesting about him!

Ghid and Fraed Enstikla
1.We managed to obtain a “blood sample”:
1.We managed to obtain a “blood sample” from the Hand at no small price. Our agent confirms that there was originally liquid in the vial, but it quickly dissipated when removed from the Cortex region.

2. Theories that the hand is attached to a larger body are unsubstantiated. Nobody has seen any evidence of this, so we assume it is disembodied.

3. The hand was first sighted around the time of Cosmo’s arrival, leading us to believe it is a telekinetic projection crafted by his own psychic abilities.

4. My security guard, Blett, surprised me with an astute observation: “If Cosmo is indeed the originator, why isn’t it a giant paw?”

5. My other security guard, Gunpt, countered with an equally astute observation: “Because he’s a flarkin’ dog. Could look like the hand of his previous owner.”
I lived with the shame of my inaction fo:
I lived with the shame of my inaction for far too long. If I had been faster, perhaps my village would have survived.

No longer. I will fight my way into Ultath. I have stalked this terrible beast for many cycles. He nearly killed me. I nearly killed him. And still the hunt continues. We each bear scars to show our rival's strength.

I have found the beast's den. I believe it led me to it. It wants to die in a place it knows well. If I am to fall, it will be here on Maklu. Another world, far from home. Far from my family. 

But we will be reunited. My actions here ensure it.
We are finally rid of the horrible beast:
We are finally rid of the horrible beast and its vile curse! We launched it right into space!

For centuries, it has poisoned these lands, devouring our people. Spreading its plague. We have tried to kill it many times. We tried fire. Spears. Holy relics. Decapitation. Dismemberment. Explosives. Yet, within days, we inevitably hear its horrible howls. Wendiiiiigo! Wendiiiiigo! Gah! It always comes back from death!

Those it bites also become beasts, but at least those can be killed. Sadly, five members of our team got bitten during its capture. They knew the risk and they know their tragic fate. Thanks to project “A.F.,” we now have a solution--an experimental craft will find it a new home. Remote. Without people. We hope the curse will transfer to new, alien soil. Our ill-fated teammates will steer the ship far beyond our solar system. May they find safe passage into the beyond.
Chondu - we made a major miscalculation:
Chondu - we made a major miscalculation choosing Maklu IV as a processing site. As it turns out, the mythological dragon is real. I know that news will please you, but it devoured and mutilated all of our hired help and most of our supplies. This is all covered by the risk clause in the contract, of course. 

Don't worry about me. My orb took a hit, but we've shipped enough hides to our contact on Knowhere to cover any repairs. 

Tell Nagan I may have found a suitable body for him--far superior to those smelly Gorilla suits he wears. I do expect extra compensation for my efforts.
You want HOW MUCH for these things?! Whe:
You want HOW MUCH for these things?! When I said "matching gold costumes," I meant gold-colored, not actual krutacking gold. We want potential clients to think we've got wealth, not wear it right on our sleeves! That makes us a target!

Here's the deal, when the time's right, we'll give these costumes a test run. If they survive it without any holes, I'll settle up with you at say... 6 percent of what you're asking. Best I can do.

They look flarking amazing, by the way.
Marked “Guardians of the Galaxy,” these: Marked “Guardians of the Galaxy,” these business cards were delivered to every major spaceport in the galaxy. While many arrived through various types of postal systems, there were several incidents of air drops as well. The Garamux station went on full lockdown, believing they were under attack, and has permanently banished the self-described “heroes-for-hire” group. A Nova Corps strategist studied the deployment methods used and concluded, “if you wanted to deliver a biological weapon on a massive scale, this is how you’d do it.”
This childhood toy represents a strange:
This childhood toy represents a strange brown creature called Chewbacca from a popular entertainment franchise on Earth. Nova Corps Centurion Ko-Rel describes the object in a Hala’s Hope possessions report: 
“A child’s toy. No toxic materials or weapon functions. It was the childhood toy of Peter Jason Quill, also known as Star-Lord. His Chitauri captors confiscated it, but for some reason he went back for it, as well as for his other possessions, before escaping. He said it used to have something called a “bowcaster” that was chewed up by an Earth beast called a Kubrick.”
Ancient Katathian blades were usually fo:
Ancient Katathian blades were usually forged from ultra-dense ore, deep-mined from the planet’s nearest moon. Since proper Katathian weapons retain their edges even after hacking through armor or bone, they are often passed down through generations. They are bestowed upon the worthy through austere coming of age rituals, creating a solemn, life-long bond between the two.

According to tradition, warriors do not keep the names of their inherited weapons, nor do they rename them. Instead, they discover what the steel wishes to be called through battle. Drax has not yet discovered the names of his blades but is watching for omens and portents. It could be the writing on a wall, the last sound of a dying foe, or a particular pattern of arterial spray.
Rocket’s BBE is an ion cartridge-fed, he: Rocket’s BBE is an ion cartridge-fed, heavy automatic weapon originally based on Kree infantry rifles but modified beyond recognition (and reason). Compressed gas instead of a mechanical system allows for an incredibly high rate of fire and minimizes jamming. However, it is jammed full of other guns, some of them far bigger than the core weapon. Rocket appears to have installed a pocket dimension generator directly into his weapon, allowing it to unfold and expand in impossible ways. It does not currently possess a safety trigger.
Groot’s back-mounted harness was hand-cr: Groot’s back-mounted harness was hand-crafted by Rocket, who assembled it out of pieces from a stolen Halfword ship. The harness has special sentimental value not only because it represents both Rocket’s freedom from torturous experiments and his bond with his best friend, but also because it lets him tower high above the battlefield and snipe scutholes without mercy.
Known to pirates and raiders as a Nova C: Known to pirates and raiders as a Nova Corps "disabler" and/or "tracker," the 7A-13 is a timed power termination lock used as encouragement to pay fines before their deadline. If the countdown expires or somebody tampers with the lock, a surge of Nova Force energy will fry the ship’s navigation system and send a tracking signal to the Worldmind. Fortunately, it will not impact life support systems.
The chances of winning Knowhere’s lotter: The chances of winning Knowhere’s lottery are astronomical. Using quantum-kiosk technology, tickets are sold across the galaxy, allowing trillions of entries for each draw and making its owners unthinkable profits. However, nobody knows exactly where those profits go. Nova Corps has tried to investigate the operation several times, but always backs down under pressure from Knowhere’s security chief, Cosmo.
These devices, frequently sold in Knowhe:
These devices, frequently sold in Knowhere’s black market, appear to be replicas of Nova Force locking system keys. With the original key, Corpsman can attach and remove a ship-disabling tracker from impounded and temporarily released vessels.

This replica is significantly lighter than its source and makes a disturbing rattle when shaken. Note that tampering with a Nova Force lock can permanently damage a ship and can also lead to more fines.
Ride safe with Skaggler! \n\nSkaggler is:
Ride safe with Skaggler! 

Skaggler is the cosmic saint of safe travel. It’s not uncommon to find one of these little dolls on the cluttered dash of interstellar freight haulers. Their manufacturer, Gumdy’s Gumplings, worried about a brand hit when Knowhere cartels started leaving these little guys at bloody crime scenes. Much to their surprise, business is booming now that the market has expanded.
Kree experimental weapon engineers craft: Kree experimental weapon engineers crafted the spinal control unit on Halfworld to command and control the local animal population, transforming them into killing machines. An extensive series of genetic manipulations, augmented limbs, and neurosurgery turned the wild animals into living weapons, but the control cage primarily reinforced the defiance/punishment response with an extremely painful shock right to the nervous system. In the case of a completely defiant test subject, operators could take full control of the subject and pilot them manually. The unit is also equipped with an implosion bomb to remove all traces of evidence and technology, should the subject be caught.
The Galactic Assassin’s Guild ring, gran: The Galactic Assassin’s Guild ring, granted only to members with at least fifty kills on their record, is as deadly as those who wear it. It is lined with tiny compartments that can produce spikes with various pre-loaded poisons, each designed to have maximum destructive impact on a specific race. A simple brush across the back of the neck is enough to kill most targets. The ring responds to motion, specifically hand gestures that the assassin can set before the mission. It also allows one preset suicide gesture, which will inject every poison into the wielder’s finger. The Guild recommends choosing a gesture that cannot accidentally be recreated through normal activity.
The sacred blade of Xatar the Unfinished:
The sacred blade of Xatar the Unfinished. Xatar was a warrior-king of the Katathian people whose death is used as an example of how one must find purpose to reach Ultath (paradise). Xatar was initially shamed for his crushing defeat at the hands of a rival king. Upon requesting a duel to the death, which would grant Xatar his place in Ultath, his captor refused. Instead, Xatar was banished and broken.

Xatar refused to give up. Together with a band of his defeated people, he led a great pilgrimage to Maklu IV, where they would hunt the fearsome Kakarantharan dragon, Fin Fang Foom. They stood no chance, but they died gloriously. With purpose.

Many Katathians have forged their own blades to look like Xatar’s, hoping to earn a meaningful death and join the legendary king in Ultath.
Universal translation technology has adv: Universal translation technology has advanced exponentially since its creation, replacing the old handheld models with earpieces and even cerebral implants. Most models contain, at minimum, at least all 7,215 “core” languages of interstellar diplomacy. However, those with more wealth can procure more obscure and even defunct languages if they so desire. The cerebral implant also serves to alter the perception of lip movements, a great benefit for those who read lips as well as those easily confused by the desynchronization between speaker and voice.
Lamentis’ Priests of Pama use these ston:
Lamentis’ Priests of Pama use these stones as they train to unlock inner wisdom through deep meditation rituals. Their mantra, spoken in an ancient Kree dialect, roughly translates to:

I AM OUTSIDE THE STONE, LOOKING IN.
I PUSH UPON THE SURFACE OF THE STONE.
THE STONE CRACKS, ALLOWING ME PASSAGE.
I AM INSIDE THE STONE, LOOKING OUT.
I AM THE STONE.
SHOO SHOO CHA KOO.
An ancient technological device unearthe:
An ancient technological device unearthed by a deep space mining colony. Their chief scientist, Raker, submitted the artifact to the Galactic Science Committee for study, but they were unable to discern its origin or its function. They did conclude that it was potentially an aerosol delivery system, perhaps even a weapon. They advised Raker to dispose of the device.

One of the GSC researchers dissented and believes it to be a Badoon egg warmer. The Committee denied his request for further study.
The Glarnots were a group of rebels and:
The Glarnots were a group of rebels and jewel thieves on Sgundor Dwide, where it perpetually rains diamonds. However, the powerful Sgundoran “weathermen,” with their ability to track and secure storms, control the planet’s wealth, profiting from diamond exports while the rest of the population fights for food. Hiding their identities behind carved masks, the Glarnots began to raid diamond operations and return the wealth to their people.
They managed to steal about five diamonds before they were captured and set to be publicly executed with diamond-tip lances. In their final speech, the Glarnots urged the citizens to resist, and to take back what was rightfully theirs. Then they were killed. The Sgundoran diamond trade remains as strong as ever and possession of a Glarnot mask is now punishable by death.
The Makluvian deeproot is an exceptional: The Makluvian deeproot is an exceptionally hardy plant, able to thrive well below the planet’s frozen surface for many rotations before having to push a limb up to absorb sunlight. Even the smallest piece of the deeproot can regrow an entirely new plant on just about any other habitable world. Because their regenerative abilities are so rapid, many cultures use the deeproot as a key ingredient in medicine. However, import and export rules are enforced to prevent the predatory plant from spreading and annihilating the rest of the planet’s flora.
The Universal Church of Truth’s new “Mat:
The Universal Church of Truth’s new “Matriarch” has been observed wielding a mysterious amber-hued gem. Although Nova Corps has only scattered and wildly varying reports, witnesses claim to have seen her channeling her “faith” power through it and transforming defiant captives into willing servants.

It appears to be the same stone previously embedded in the forehead of the Church’s first “divine vessel,” Adam Warlock, also known as "Him." Little is known about the gem, its origin wrapped in mystery just like its former owner. It appears to be an artifact of immense power, once glowing brilliantly as Warlock healed the sick. First-hand accounts describe a disastrous separation between the gem and its bearer, who believed it was feeding on souls and corrupting his own.
The notorious pirate group known as the: The notorious pirate group known as the Ravagers were infamous for relentlessly pursuing their prey, punching holes in the victim’s ship, and eventually boarding. Their communications bracelets served to report their progress to the waiting squadron, helped them to track rare materials on the ship, and generated bursts of directional EMP to short out defensive systems or locks. The Ravagers were highly protective of their bracelets, threatening death to any who tried to steal them. However, since the capture of the Ravagers’ leader, Yondu Udonta, the devices have begun to show up on the black market.

Some of them far more advanced and some of them struggling as we did. We were welcomed with open arms by a group calling themselves the Nova Corps.

To our horror, we learned the galaxy itself is currently at war. Beeldar is right in the path of the aggressors, a violent race called the Chitauri. We requested aid from our new allies, but their rescue force will soon be intercepted by a much larger Chitauri fleet. We have decided to rapidly burn our fuel reserves to reach the Chitauri first. In our naivete, we do not have weapons on the Starborus, but she is fast, and she is built strong. We will ram their capital ship. Perhaps we can save our new friends.

Know this—for a brief, incredible moment, Beeldar found peace. We accomplished everything we set out to do. I pray our sacrifice will make a difference in our final hour.

The shollock is a nasty creature from Ch:
The shollock is a nasty creature from Chitauri Prime that is often used as an interrogation tool. Its original name, “chaa lloghk” translates roughly to “screaming chair,” but not for any sound the creature makes. Captured Resistance soldiers during the Galactic War feared being “shollocked” by the enemy, and for good reason. The Chitauri appear to have bred these beasts to have larger spikes and sharper edges than nature intended.

Normally kept secure in the belly of a Chitauri vessel, many shollocks were set loose upon the enemy if the ship was about to be lost to a boarding party.
These unusual creatures are found exclus:
These unusual creatures are found exclusively in Nova Corps’ post-war wreckage dump, the Quarantine Zone. The fact that they were never seen before led scientists to believe it was a mutation caused by the radiation and toxic substances within the crashed ships. Genetic analysis concluded that the moniscobule was originally a Huskian spindlerat, a common breed of vermin found aboard many deep spaceships. This mutation has increased its size tenfold and distorted its body to the point where it is unrecognizable.

Nova Corps has assured scientists that these unfortunate beasts will be sealed away and destroyed with the rest of the hazardous contents of the Quarantine Zone bubble.
The Priests of Pama have described Lamen:
The Priests of Pama have described Lamentis’ “Languishing Fog” in mystical terms, which is not particularly useful for xenobiologists. They say it is alive and that it follows them as they travel the tunnels below the surface. They also claim it seeps into the mind and exposes one’s inner turmoil or awakens one’s inner eyes.

But they seem to be hiding something more sinister. Off-worlders have met with some of the priests who have encountered this fog and found them to be in a near-vegetative state, barely able to utter words and unable to care for themselves. One cotati warned visitors that the fog was a psychic parasite before the priests silenced him.

Is this mysterious vapor a toxic hallucinogen? If it stalks its prey like the priests have described, then surely it is alive.
Got some real bad news for you, sis. The:
Got some real bad news for you, sis. Them critters you had me smuggle off of Crackgh II? You didn’t tell me they bred like Seknarfian mudhogs. I got a cargo bay full of the ugly flarkers and they grew up FAST. I can hear them banging on the walls and shrieking something fierce. Probably hungry. When I saw my fuel was leaking, I put two and two together and realized they’re chewing up my fuel lines. 

To make it worse, I gotta fly right through a Nova Creeps blockade. I ain’t got no way to hide them things, so I’m thinking about scuttling this old heap and taking my shuttle to Knowhere. Expect a bill for a new ship soon and we can figure out our next haul. I know you’re good for it. 

What can I say? Scut happens.
My heart, do not come back to Hala. Ther:
My heart, do not come back to Hala. There is nothing here for you. I fear it will soon fall as so many other worlds have. Kree-Lar is in flames. Most of the spaceports have been decimated. The Chitauri have gathered many of our remaining leaders and have announced public executions. Fear not, we escaped—we are on a Shi’ar mercy ship and headed for refuge. Those monsters are focused on destroying our cities. So far, they are not pursuing us. We will survive this, even if our beautiful Hala does not.

Continue your work on Halfworld. I beg of you, demand that your leaders unleash everything they have to make these monsters suffer. Every unfinished machine. Every experimental weapon. All of it. Right into the heart of Chitauri Prime. Show them the superior might of the Kree Empire! Make your children proud!
That’s the genius of it, see? We’ve got:
That’s the genius of it, see? We’ve got all the monsters' DNA profiles loaded in the system. Any of the Queen’s pets get loose and into the airducts, which they love for some flarkin’ reason, when the drones find them, all that do is stun them based on the profile. Makes it easier to get them back in their cages.

Not in the system, you die. End up splattered on the walls. Simple as that.

Just make sure you keep the profiles up to date. Last thing you want is the latest getting loose and dying. Hellbender’ll flay you alive if that happens. Ask Hurunn'Ol. If you can find any bits of him willing to talk.

Add your sample to the system too, in case you ever find yourself hunting down a mistake you made.
That’s it. I’ve had it. \n\nIf I’ve said:
That’s it. I’ve had it. 

If I’ve said it once, I’ve said it a quintillion times.

DO NOT JUMP IN THE KRUTACKIN’ ELEVATOR!

This is the seventh service request. Seventh! 

I’m officially sending a formal complaint to the Worldmind. Let’s see how those high-and-mighty Corpsmen like a big fat reprimand on their records.

I can’t believe I joined the Corps for this.
What does a fatally wounded wuruum and M:
What does a fatally wounded wuruum and Mantlo’s Bar on Knowhere Station have in common? Both are in the midst of a slow and painful death. 

Do not get me wrong, loyal reader. I came to Knowhere on a mission. But even I, a connoisseur of dive bars and flark-ridden watering holes, cannot be swayed to give a full skull to this garishly lit den of thievery that has the audacity to call itself a bar.

For a bar suggests that there is one by which to be rated against. If Mantlo’s has a bar, it has sunk so low into the rotting celestial grey matter that it cannot – dare I say will not – be found again.

Therefore, reader, I must caution you. Drink at your own risk, lest you, too, be consumed by the slow entropy of irrelevance. A generous 0.5 out of 5555555555jksjdnhnallllllllllllllddddddddskaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
All I know is they told us we were leavi:
All I know is they told us we were leaving the Quarantine Zone. Even though we still had rotations left out there. At first I was glad. Thought maybe we'd hit our furlough. But then it started. I don't know where it started, but it crept through the ship.

People started to change. We thought it was a virus at first. Maybe that's why we left the QZ. But it got worse. They wanted people to convert to something? We tried contacting New Xandar, but the Worldmind wouldn't answer. 

Not long after, they started killing each other.

A few of us made for the escape pods, but they were waiting, or right on our heels. They were everywhere. Some of us escaped. I said I'd stay behind. Give them a chance. 

I hear them over the comms, talking about some Matriarch. Maybe I can keep hiding, but I don't think I have much longer. Everything hurts, and I just want the hurting to stop...
As you are all aware, the Accuser will b:
As you are all aware, the Accuser will be making her diplomatic trip to Hala’s Hope next cycle to discuss the Kree Council's involvement with reconstruction efforts. However, this is not her only business on the station. All Kree currently serving Nova Corps will be expected to meet with the Accuser at the allotted time for your interrogation.

You may be asked to provide records of family history and recent medical results – not the ones provided by Nova Corps, but by a certified Kree physician from the Purity Council list. If you have children currently living with you, they may be interviewed as well.

Failure to arrive for your appointment will not be tolerated. The Accuser will be more than willing to locate you in your place of work and escort you to an interrogation room. Do be punctual.
I lived with the shame of my inaction fo:
I lived with the shame of my inaction for far too long. If I had been faster, perhaps my village would have survived.

No longer. I will fight my way into Ultath. I have stalked this terrible beast for many cycles. He nearly killed me. I nearly killed him. And still the hunt continues. We each bear scars to show our rival's strength.

I have found the beast's den. I believe it led me to it. It wants to die in a place it knows well. If I am to fall, it will be here on Maklu. Another world, far from home. Far from my family. 

But we will be reunited. My actions here ensure it.
Chondu - we made a major miscalculation:
Chondu - we made a major miscalculation choosing Maklu IV as a processing site. As it turns out, the mythological dragon is real. I know that news will please you, but it devoured and mutilated all of our hired help and most of our supplies. This is all covered by the risk clause in the contract, of course. 

Don't worry about me. My orb took a hit, but we've shipped enough hides to our contact on Knowhere to cover any repairs. 

Tell Nagan I may have found a suitable body for him--far superior to those smelly Gorilla suits he wears. I do expect extra compensation for my efforts.
Ride safe with Skaggler! \n\nSkaggler is:
Ride safe with Skaggler! 

Skaggler is the cosmic saint of safe travel. It’s not uncommon to find one of these little dolls on the cluttered dash of interstellar freight haulers. Their manufacturer, Gumdy’s Gumplings, worried about a brand hit when Knowhere cartels started leaving these little guys at bloody crime scenes. Much to their surprise, business is booming now that the market has expanded.
Lamentis’ Priests of Pama use these ston:
Lamentis’ Priests of Pama use these stones as they train to unlock inner wisdom through deep meditation rituals. Their mantra, spoken in an ancient Kree dialect, roughly translates to:

I AM OUTSIDE THE STONE, LOOKING IN.
I PUSH UPON THE SURFACE OF THE STONE.
THE STONE CRACKS, ALLOWING ME PASSAGE.
I AM INSIDE THE STONE, LOOKING OUT.
I AM THE STONE.
SHOO SHOO CHA KOO.
